title: Materials Process Operator
description:
It's exciting to work for a company that makes the world measurably better.

We're committed to bringing safety, quality, and customer focus to the business of advanced ceramics manufacturing.

Job Title

Materials Process Operator

Utilizing manual and automated equipment, processes raw materials into high-quality ceramic powders for use in producing finished goods. Automation systems are highly process integrated and apply to routine and repeatable production processes in support of their efficient operation.

Roles & Responsibilities:

  • Follow all Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) procedures as required. Identify opportunities for safety improvements.
  • Performs startups, shutdowns and product mix changes across standardized production processes with manual and basic automation components
  • Identify technical problems and implement routine or directed solutions
  • Follows documented and scheduled maintenance procedures
  • Follow routine and repeatable work instructions and product mix specifications and may encounter special instructions in the preparation of ceramic material.
  • Learns and applies manufacturing principles and best practices as the method to most effectively complete their work.
  • Work closely with other operators to share information for production continuity between shifts, process steps or departments
  • Perform in-process quality testing for assigned process area
  • Safely operate powered industrial equipment to move material to and from locations within the facility.
  • Maintain workspace cleanliness and follow appropriate 6S practices.
  • Assist in accurately tracking all inventory, supplies, and raw materials.

Job Requirements:

Education:

  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • Basic reading and math skills
  • Must meet all training requirements as defined by department

Experience:

  • 1-2 years of manufacturing experience a plus
  • Forklift operation required, experience a plus
  • Semi-automated machine operation experience preferred

Functional/Technical Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

  • Communication: Shares information, ideas, feelings, and observations clearly, while also taking the time to listen and respond to others.
  • Technology Use: Ability and willingness to learn and navigate various devices and software programs including touch screen technology
  • Mechanical Aptitude: Basic mechanical aptitude including selection and use of hand and power tools
  • Detail Oriented: Ability to understand and act on verbal and written instructions to complete tasks with increasing accuracy and thoroughness.
  • Time Management: Effectively uses time and proactively follows priorities to meet set targets

Position Specific Physical Requirements

  • Ability to lift 60 lbs.
  • Ability to work from ladders when performing tasks.
  • Must be able to climb and descend stairs throughout work shift.
  • Must be able to work in a cold or hot work environment.
  • May be exposed to a wet or dusty work environment.

title: Education Pathway Specialist
location: 7110 N FRESNO ST SUITE 300 - FRESNO, CA 93720
description:
About California Teaching Fellows Foundation:

California Teaching Fellows Foundation (CTFF) is a nonprofit dedicated to developing passionate individuals into expanded learning tutoring roles that directly support TK-12th grade students across the 6 counties we serve. By investing in our Teaching Fellows' growth, we build a sustainable pipeline of future educators who are deeply rooted and committed to the communities they call home.

Our Mission: ELEVATE and EQUIP educators to EMPOWER youth, communities, and themselves.

Our Vision: Teaching Fellows emerge as credentialed teachers and leaders in education and beyond. Students feel seen, supported, and inspired to build their own path. Communities are rooted in the belief that education creates opportunities and hope.

The Opportunity:

Education Pathway Program Leadership (25%)

Lead the planning, coordination, and implementation of education pathway programs, including FAAME (Future African American Male Educators), Future Fellows, Formando el Futuro, Road to Teaching (RTT), the Summer Internship Program, college campus visits and Professional Development Opportunities (e.g., Burton PD), as well as the Annual Signing Day. Ensure all programs are implemented with fidelity and meet outcomes as outlined in grant funding or partnership agreements. Plan and execute high-quality events and conferences, including student academies, regional convenings, and public-facing showcases. Support event logistics such as securing venues, coordinating speakers and vendors, arranging materials, and managing registration. Ensure all events remain within budget, meet attendance targets, and provide impactful, mission-aligned experiences for participants. Administer surveys for data collection and analyze feedback.

Administrative/Data Collection (25%)

Will be responsible for research and updating Pathways to Teaching website to ensure all information is up to date. This role will also need to coordinate with the Community Development (CD) specialist on Ed Pathways web series. They will schedule guest speakers for the show along with coordinating filming days and times with the CD Specialist. This position will also require collaboration with our IT team for data collection purposes and create a quarterly snapshot of Education Pathway touchpoints with our Teaching Fellows and external partners. Lastly, this individual will help research and develop content for the Education Pathway quarterly newsletter that is distributed to our Teaching Fellows.

District and School Site Coordination (20%)

Oversee student participation and program delivery across key district partners, including Lemoore, Burton, Corcoran, Firebaugh, Caruthers, Valley ROP (Professional Development and summer internship), and Clovis Unified (Summer Internship focus). Serve approximately 150 Future Fellows and coordinate conferences with up to 350 attendees. Maintain regular communication with district administrators, site leaders, and mentors to ensure smooth program operations and high-quality student engagement.

Partnership Management (10%)

Act as liaison between district, higher education, and community partners.Maintain strong working relationships with partner representatives to ensure alignment and program success. Attend and contribute to advisory committee meetings and district partner discussions to support collaborative program improvement.

Staff and Mentor Oversight (10%)

Provide supervision, support, and development opportunities for mentors, Teachers on Special Assignment (TOSAs), and instructional personnel participating in pathway programs. Organize and facilitate required trainings, including mentor orientation, Future Fellow Academy (FFA), and district-designated or grant-funded sessions. Monitor performance and provide ongoing coaching and feedback to ensure program excellence.

Talent and Recruitment Collaboration (10%)

Collaborate with the Talent Acquisition team to identify and refer promising candidates discovered through pathway programs. Support long-term educator pipeline strategies by fostering student interest in teaching careers. Ensure program participants are well-informed about CTFF opportunities and advancement pathways.

title: Optical Technician / Optician
description:
PERKS

  • Full Benefits Package - Medical, Vision, Dental and Life Insurance
  • 401k + Employer Matching
  • Paid Time Off (PTO) and Paid Holidays
  • Paid Maternity Leave
  • Eyecare Certification Reimbursement
  • Competitive Base Pay
  • Employee Discounts

SUMMARY

An Optical Technician will achieve a world class Total Patient Experience that maximizes retail sales while also supporting the patients’ medical needs. This team member is trained to dispense and fit glasses and contacts, working from the prescriptions written by Optometrists and Ophthalmologists. They connect the patient's needs to the goods and services offered.


LOCATION

  • Work is primarily performed in a standard office or clinical setting. However, travel to other locations may be required to carry out essential job duties and responsibilities

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Embrace and execute our Total Patient Experience to build relationships with all patients while delivering great medical support
  • Determine patient wants and needs and selling to exceed their expectations
  • Assist patients in selecting frames according to style and color, coordinating frames with facial and eye measurements and optical prescriptions
  • Able to operate the auto-lensometer and manual lensometer
  • Educate and recommend specific lenses, lens coatings and frames to suit patient needs
  • Can accurately collect measurements such as bridge, eye size, temple length, seg heights, vertex distance, pupillary distance, and pantoscopic tilt
  • Dispense patient orders and repair and adjust patient frames
  • Dispense all glasses and/or contact lens orders using current process

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Previous medical office experience preferred; previous ophthalmic experience strongly preferred.
  • Minimum of 1 year in a position interacting with customers/patients or the equivalent combination of education and experience
  • Favorable result on background check as required by state
  • Must be able to provide proof of identity and right to work in the United States

EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE

  • High school diploma or GED required

LICENSES AND CREDENTIALS

title: Senior Director, AI Research
description:
Job Description

What is the opportunity?

RBC's AI Group is building the future of AI-powered banking, and our research teams are at the forefront of this transformation. Reporting to the VP, Applied AI Research & Solutions, the Senior Director, AI Research will lead a team of world-class machine learning researchers and research engineers to develop cutting-edge AI algorithms that directly power RBC's products and services.

This is a unique opportunity to bridge frontier AI research with real-world business impact. You'll work at the intersection of innovation and application by translating the latest advances in machine learning into production-ready solutions that serve millions of clients across credit, fraud detection, market intelligence, pricing optimization, and generative AI applications.

As a member of RBC Borealis AI, you'll leverage RBC's unique data assets and strategic partnerships to push the boundaries of what's possible in AI, while ensuring your work delivers measurable business value aligned with RBC's $1 billion AI ambition.

What will you do?

AI Research Leadership:

  • Lead and mentor a high-performing team of AI researchers and research engineers, fostering a culture of innovation, collaboration, and impact-driven solutions.
  • Direct the development of novel machine learning algorithms and models across one or more domains: credit risk, fraud detection, market prediction, pricing & optimization, or generative/agentic AI. Leverage RBC and external data to deliver differentiating solutions and intellectual property to the business.
  • Define AI roadmaps with ML models that balance advancing the state-of-the-art with delivering tangible business outcomes aligned to RBC's strategic priorities.
  • Build and retain top-tier AI talent by creating an environment that attracts leading researchers from both academia and industry.
  • Act as a thought leader and partner to RBC businesses and functions and advise on the art of the possible for AI in these domains.
  • Evaluate new areas for AI investment, complete proof of concept testing and evaluation.

Applied Research & Business Impact:

  • Partner closely with the VP, AI Research and Innovation team to operationalize frontier research and translate breakthroughs into applied solutions.
  • Collaborate with VP, Solutions Engineering & Delivery to ensure AI algorithms are production-ready, scalable, and integrated seamlessly into RBC's enterprise platforms.
  • Drive rapid experimentation and iteration to test and validate models against real-world business problems, ensuring measurable ROI.
  • Develop intellectual property and publish research findings that position RBC as a thought leader in AI innovation.

Cross-Functional Collaboration:

  • Act as a trusted technical advisor to business partners across RBC's lines of business, translating complex AI concepts into actionable insights.
  • Work with platform teams to leverage RBC's AI & data infrastructure (Lumina) for model development, training, and deployment.
  • Partner with AI Governance & Evaluation teams to ensure all models meet regulatory, ethical, and compliance standards.
  • Engage with external research communities, academic institutions, and industry partners to stay ahead of emerging AI trends and technologies.
  • Champion responsible AI practices, embedding fairness, transparency, and bias mitigation into the research lifecycle.
  • Identify opportunities to advance RBC's AI capabilities through experimentation with emerging technologies (e.g., foundation models, multimodal AI, reinforcement learning).
  • Contribute to RBC's AI thought leadership through publications, patents, conference presentations, and community engagement.
  • In this role, you will communicate and interact frequently with RBC partners and/or employees located across Canada and/or worldwide.

What do you need to succeed?

Must Have:

  • PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, Mathematics, or a related field, or equivalent industry experience.
  • 10+ years of experience developing and deploying machine learning models in industry settings, with at least 3-5 years in leadership roles and people management.
  • Experience translating research prototypes into production-grade solutions at scale, preferably in regulated industries (financial services, healthcare, etc.).
  • Strong publication record and recognized thought leadership in AI/ML (conference papers, patents, technical blogs, or open-source contributions).
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate across technical and non-technical stakeholders, communicating complex concepts clearly to senior leadership.

What's in it for you?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

  • Work at the cutting edge of AI: Access to RBC's unique data assets, world-class compute infrastructure, and strategic partnerships with leading AI research institutions.
  • Industry-leading research environment: Publish your work, attend top-tier conferences, and collaborate with renowned researchers from RBC Borealis and beyond.
  • Real-world impact: Your research will directly power products and services used by millions of clients across Canada and globally.
  • Comprehensive Total Rewards Program including competitive compensation, bonuses, flexible benefits, and stock options.
  • Talent development: Leaders who support your growth through coaching, mentorship, and opportunities to shape RBC's AI strategy.
  • Dynamic, high-performing team: Work alongside some of the brightest minds in AI, machine learning, and financial services.
  • Opportunities for progressively greater impact: Shape the future of AI at one of the world's leading financial institutions.

title: Senior Principal, Enterprise Strategy & Strategic Opportunities
description:
The Senior Principal, Enterprise Strategy & Strategic Opportunities is a senior leader within Enterprise Strategy, Ventures & Innovation responsible for shaping and advancing high-value enterprise and business strategies. The role will own a portfolio of consequential opportunities and unresolved strategic questions, with primary focus on critical problem solving, business opportunities, and new growth and business innovation. The Senior Principal will turn broad, ambiguous questions into clear strategic choices, opportunity cases, and executive-ready recommendations that drive enterprise value.

The Senior Principal will also provide senior leadership capacity across the broader Enterprise Strategy agenda, including enterprise strategic positioning and competitive strategy and enterprise-choice work, long-term enterprise strategy and strategic priorities strategy development, and selected strategic planning priorities. The role will operate across enterprise trade-offs, portfolio implications, and cross-business opportunities, regularly engaging ELT members, business unit and corporate function and shared services leaders, and other senior stakeholders. Two positions may be hired against this common role profile, with portfolios flexed over time based on enterprise priorities, individual strengths, and demand.

This leader is expected to combine strong external orientation, strategic judgment, commercial insight, and the ability to lead through influence. The Senior Principal will autonomously drive major bodies of work, mobilize cross-functional teams, build trusted relationships across the enterprise, and serve as a thought partner to senior leadership on opportunities, risks, and new solutions.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Opportunities & Critical Problem Solving

  • Own a portfolio of the most important unresolved enterprise or business questions and convert broad asks into structured, decision-ready strategic options.

  • Identify and evaluate growth opportunities, strategic adjacencies, partnerships, capability plays, and business development pathways that can create meaningful enterprise value.

  • Lead rigorous problem framing, issue-tree development, strategic and economic analysis, scenario assessment, and recommendation development.

  • Clarify enterprise trade-offs, value-creation logic, risks, dependencies, and execution requirements for senior leadership decisions.

  • Mobilize and lead cross-functional teams and flexible strategy pods, maintaining pace, quality, and alignment from question definition through leadership decision.

New Growth and Business Innovation

  • Shape new growth and business innovation strategies that create new growth, strengthen scaled core businesses, or evolve future business models.

  • Identify opportunities where new propositions, channels, partnerships, technologies, capabilities, or combinations of enterprise assets can improve customer value, economics, growth, or long-term advantage.

  • Develop innovation and opportunity theses, future-state models, growth platforms, and incubation or investment logic.

  • Partner with business units, innovation, Corporate Development, Finance, and enterprise leaders to pressure-test concepts, build opportunity cases, and determine which ideas merit further investment or action.

  • Move beyond idea identification by defining the strategic path, critical choices, evidence requirements, and early actions needed to advance priority opportunities.

Enterprise Strategic Positioning, Long-Term Strategy & Enterprise Direction Support

  • Lead or support high-consequence enterprise strategic positioning and competitive strategy and enterprise-choice work involving where the enterprise plays, where value shifts, which moves matter, and what trade-offs leadership must make.

  • Help steward and advance long-term enterprise strategy and strategic priorities by translating the enterprise direction into sharper choices, priorities, guardrails, growth hooks, and implications for businesses and corporate functions and shared services.

  • Develop portfolio, pathway, competitive-position, and strategic-option analyses for Board and ELT discussions.

  • Integrate external, customer, competitor, financial, and internal capability perspectives to challenge assumptions and strengthen enterprise recommendations.

  • Partner with the VP of Enterprise Strategy and other senior strategy leaders on sensitive, confidential, and highly ambiguous priorities.

Strategic Planning & Cross-Team Leadership

  • Provide senior strategy capacity to selected planning priorities, including challenging business strategies, testing strategic assumptions, and synthesizing implications across businesses and corporate functions and shared services.

  • Partner with the Strategic Planning & Integration Lead to connect opportunity and innovation work to enterprise priorities, planning choices, and strategy-linked financial considerations.

  • Contribute to enterprise planning reviews, leadership forums, and Board readiness where applied strategy expertise is required.

  • Maintain durable ownership of assigned strategy lanes while deploying flexibly across the Enterprise Strategy portfolio as needs evolve.

  • Help prioritize and deploy supporting talent across projects and develop Principals and Advisors through clear direction, coaching, and high-quality feedback.

External Insight, Relationships & Executive Influence

  • Maintain a deeply external perspective on healthcare markets, customer and employer needs, competitors, policy, technology, capital flows, and emerging business models.

  • Identify external developments that create enterprise opportunities, risks, strategic inflection points, or the need for new solutions.

  • Build trusted relationships and an active network across business units, enterprise corporate functions and shared services, Corporate Development, Finance, innovation, peer groups, the Strategy Community, and senior leadership.

  • Engage leaders to sharpen questions, surface diverse perspectives, create alignment, and improve the quality and speed of strategic decisions.

  • Develop compelling executive narratives, presentations, and communications and represent Enterprise Strategy in leadership and cross-functional forums.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor's degree required; MBA or other relevant advanced degree strongly preferred.

  • 10+ years of experience in corporate strategy, management consulting, business development, investment banking, private equity, innovation, or related strategic leadership roles.

  • Demonstrated success leading enterprise-level strategy development, growth strategy, critical problem solving, or business opportunity work in complex organizations.

  • Proven ability to autonomously lead ambiguous, high-consequence work and influence senior executives without direct authority.

  • Exceptional strategic thinking, external orientation, commercial judgment, structured problem-solving, and executive communication skills.

  • Strong analytical capabilities, including market and competitive assessment, business case development, financial analysis, scenario evaluation, and strategic synthesis.

  • Experience mobilizing cross-functional teams and driving alignment across matrixed organizations.

  • Proven ability to build broad, trusted relationships and navigate sensitive or confidential topics with sound judgment.

Preferred

  • Experience in healthcare, health services, insurance, pharmacy, or adjacent industries.

  • Experience in enterprise strategy, portfolio strategy, growth platforms, business model innovation, partnerships, or inorganic opportunity evaluation.

  • Experience supporting Board, ELT, or comparable senior governance discussions.

  • Demonstrated ability to develop talent and lead project teams across formal and informal reporting lines.

What Success Looks Like

  • Enterprise and business leaders receive clear, differentiated, and decision-ready strategies on the most consequential opportunities and problems.

  • New growth and business innovation priorities move from broad ideas to well-defined strategic choices, opportunity cases, and paths forward.

  • Enterprise strategic positioning and competitive strategy, long-term enterprise strategy and strategic priorities, and planning work is strengthened by rigorous external insight, enterprise judgment, and clear articulation of trade-offs.

  • The Senior Principal autonomously drives major work while creating meaningful leverage for the VP of Enterprise Strategy and other senior leaders.

  • Strong relationships across business units, corporate functions and shared services, peer groups, the Strategy Community, and senior leadership improve Enterprise Strategy’s access, influence, and impact.

  • Principals and Advisors develop through strong project leadership, coaching, and exposure to high-value strategic work.

title: Patient Transporter
description:
Transports all patient populations to and from examinations and treatments. Performs general errands and other routine duties including cleaning equipment, securing supplies, and other tasks as required. Acts as a team member in the delivery of quality patient care. Adheres to unit procedures wherever transport services rendered.

Essential Functions

  • Practicing safe lifting and techniques, transports patients by assisting patients in and out of cars, lifting patients on and off beds, moving patients to and from special services and treatment areas using wheelchairs, gurneys, or moveable beds.

  • Prepares patient for transport and performs passive and active identification to ensure all patients are properly identified before transporting.

  • Transports all patients and equipment to and from testing and procedure areas including inpatient, outpatient, emergency and high risk Intensive Care Unit (ICU).

  • Effectively communicates with medical employees to ensure all required medical supplies and medications are appropriately transported with the patient including the administering of oxygen when required.

  • Responsible for the timely discharge of patients throughout the hospital.

  • Under the direction of medical employees and/or Registered Nurse (RN), assists in providing support in toileting ambulatory patients.

  • Cleans and disinfects equipment according to established policies and procedures. Maintains clean work areas and returns equipment to appropriate department. Communicates malfunctioning equipment/instruments to appropriate department/unit staff.

  • Actively participates in safety initiatives and risk mitigating measures where appropriate and completes all position and unit safety related competencies and requirements on a timely basis.

  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Required

  • Successful completion of three months of on-the-job-training.

  • High school diploma or equivalent

  • BLS (AHA, American Heart Association) or BLS (ARC, American Red Cross) within 90 days of hire.

  • Understands and demonstrates safe lifting and transport techniques.

  • Knows and practices Universal Precautions as appropriate.

  • Demonstrated communication skills to interact with courtesy, tact, empathy, and professionalism in daily interaction with patients, their families, clinical licensed and non-licensed staff, physicians, and management.

  • Ability to understand and follow directions, ability to comply with HIPAA confidentiality requirements.

  • The ability to recognize if the patient is experiencing stress or other issues during transport and immediately seek assistance.

Preferred

  • Experience in patient transportation in an acute hospital environment.

title: Senior Research Scientist, Method Development (LC-MS)
description:
About The Role

We are seeking a highly motivated and experienced Senior Research Scientist with strong expertise in bioanalytical mass spectrometry to join our Method Development team. The successful candidate will lead the development and optimization of regulatory-ready bioanalytical methods using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) for a variety of therapeutic modalities, including small molecules, peptides, biologics, biomarkers, and oligonucleotides.


What You’ll Do Here

  • Develop and optimize robust bioanalytical methods using LC-MS/MS in compliance with regulatory standards.

  • Perform and oversee sample preparation, analysis, and data interpretation while meeting project timelines and quality expectations.

  • Investigate and resolve complex bioanalytical challenges through systematic troubleshooting, experimental design, and root-cause assessment.

  • Participate in client discussions and scientific meetings, communicating method development strategies, analytical results, and technical recommendations.

  • Prepare, review, and approve method development reports, SOPs, and other technical documentation as required.

  • Collaborate with validation and operational teams to support successful method transfer and implementation.

  • Stay current with advancements in LC-MS technologies and best practices to support continuous improvement.

  • Adhere to Health and Safety protocols, including personal protective practices and laboratory upkeep.


What You’ll Need to Succeed

  • Master’s or Ph.D. in Biochemistry, Chemistry, Analytical Chemistry, or a related discipline; a Bachelor’s degree with significant relevant experience may also be considered.

  • Typically 5-8+ years of relevant experience in LC-MS/MS bioanalysis, with demonstrated experience independently leading bioanalytical method development projects.

  • Experience in sample preparation techniques appropriate to the analyte type (e.g., protein precipitation, solid-phase extraction, immunoaffinity-based approaches, enzymatic digestion).

  • Strong scientific writing, communication, and presentation skills, with the ability to effectively communicate complex technical concepts to both scientific and non-scientific stakeholders.

title: I&E Technician - Intermediate
description:
#WeAreONEOK – Fortune 500 company. 100+ years in business. Leading midstream service provider. Safety first. Sustainable operations. Environmentally responsible. Employee focused.

JOB SUMMARY

ONEOK is seeking an Instrumentation Technician – Intermediate to support the safe, reliable operation of electrical, electronic, pneumatic, hydraulic, analyzer, measurement, control, and automation systems within ONEOK’s Natural Gas Liquids (NGL) segment. This role will install, inspect, troubleshoot, repair, calibrate, and maintain a variety of field equipment and systems, including instrumentation, switchgear, power distribution, SCADA, DCS, PLC systems, analyzers, transmitters, VFDs, motors, ESD systems, and related control equipment. The position will also maintain required records, support DOT-covered functions as applicable, and respond promptly to operating, safety, or equipment concerns.

This role is based on site in Lemont, IL and will also help support surrounding areas such as Morris and Rockford. Candidates must live within a reasonable drive time to Lemont, be able to work a Monday–Friday schedule, and participate in an on-call rotation. A company vehicle will be assigned, so a clean driving record is required.

The ideal candidate will bring hands-on instrumentation and electrical experience, with preferred exposure to switchgear and PLC programming. An associate degree or certificate in electronics, electrical engineering, or a similar field is preferred, though equivalent experience will also be considered. Successful candidates will be self-starters who take initiative, work well independently and as part of a team, communicate effectively across teams and functions, and demonstrate a strong commitment to safe work practices in high-pressure and flammable gas or liquids environments.

Job Profile Summary

Inspects and maintains and installs various electrical/electronic, pneumatic, hydraulic, analyzers, measurement, control and automation systems, and related equipment.

Essential Functions and Responsibilities

  • Install, operate, inspect, troubleshoot, repair, calibrate/adjust, and maintain the following equipment including but not limited to:
    • Gravitometers/Densitometers
    • Chromatographs
    • Telemetering systems
    • Moisture analyzers
    • ESD systems
    • Electronic odorization systems
    • AC Power distribution systems - single phase and three phase: 120V, 240V, 480V, 4160V
    • Motors
    • Switchgear
    • VFDs
    • Soft starters
    • 24V DC systems
    • Instrumentation
    • Flow computers
    • Pressure transmitters
    • Level transmitters
    • Flow transmitters
    • Temperature transmitters
    • Thermocouples
    • Meter tubes and orifice plates
    • Satellite equipment
    • Analytical equipment
    • Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system and remote terminal units and equipment
    • Distributed Control System (DCS)
    • Programmable Logic Control (PLC) systems
    • Perform preventative maintenance and/or analytical testing on compressors/engines, drivers, and auxiliary equipment
    • Maintain electrical power circuits, switch gear, and power distribution
    • Install and maintain security/intrusion systems
    • Drive and ensure maintenance is complete on company vehicle
  • Maintain and/or prepare reports and/or records including but not limited to:
    • Maintenance and repair records
    • Safety and environmental reports
    • Mechanical drawings
    • Electrical schematics and diagrams
    • Pressure readings
    • Material and supply orders
    • Loop sheets
  • Responsibilities may include Department of Transportation (DOT) covered functions, including operations, calibration documentation, maintenance, or emergency response on a pipeline. Job duties also require the employee to be alert and respond immediately to dangerous or hazardous conditions, and where impaired performance, or failure to follow safety precautions, could result in serious injury or property damage.

Education

  • Associate Degree or certificate in electronics, electrical engineering, or similar preferred. Equivalent experience also considered.

Work Experience

  • Experience in use and function of tools and equipment applicable to position including but not limited to:
    • Hand tools
    • Power tools
    • Electronic test equipment such as DVOM, amp clamp, and mega ohm meter
    • Gauges
    • Control devices
  • Experience and training related to:
    • Petroleum processing fundamentals
    • Computers and Software
    • Governmental rules & regulations
    • National Electric Code
    • Company policies and procedures including safe handling practices for flammable gases, liquids, and high pressure systems
    • Lockout Tagout
    • Reliability Based Programs

  • Experience reading and interpreting maintenance orders, mechanical and electrical drawings, P&ID’s, procedures, charts, diagrams, and equipment manuals
  • Experience preparing, processing, or verifying maintenance and repair records, safety and environmental reports, electrical schematics and diagrams, pressure readings, and material and supply orders

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Knowledge of: the use and function of reciprocating or gas turbine engines, compressors, and electronic and processing equipment applicable to position
  • Knowledge of: instrumentation, electronics, tools and control systems
  • Ability to: apply addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and algebraic formulas
  • Ability to: communicate and/or exchange written and verbal information and instructions

Licenses and Certifications

  • None required

Strength Factor Rating - Physical Demands/Requirements

  • Heavy Work - Exerting 50 to 100 pounds of force occasionally and/or 25 to 50 pounds of force frequently and/or 10 to 20 pounds of force constantly to move objects. Physical Demand requirements are in excess of those for Medium Work.

Strength Factor Description - Physical Demands/Requirements

  • Standing: Remaining on one's feet in an upright position at a work station without moving about (Frequently)
  • Walking: Moving about on foot (Frequently)
  • Sitting: Remaining in a seated position (Occasionally)
  • Lifting: Raising or lowering an object from one level to another (includes upward pulling) (Occasionally)
  • Carrying: Transporting an object, usually holding it in the hands or arms, or on the shoulder (Occasionally)
  • Pushing: Exerting force upon an object so that the object moves away from the force (Occasionally)
  • Pulling: Exerting force upon an object so that the object moves toward the force (includes jerking) (Occasionally)
  • Climbing: Ladders, Stairs (Occasionally)
  • Balancing: Maintaining body equilibrium to prevent falling (Occasionally)
  • Stooping: Bending the body downward and forward by bending the spine at the waist (Occasionally)
  • Kneeling: Bending the legs at the knees to come to rest on the knee or knees (Occasionally)

title: Lead, Development Planning, Production
description:
Space is a warfighting domain. True Anomaly seeks those with the talent and ambition to build the technology that secures it.

OUR MISSION

True Anomaly delivers decisive capabilities for space superiority. We build autonomous spacecraft, advanced payloads, mission software, and space-based interceptors — enabling the U.S. and its Allies to secure the space environment and counter threats from the ultimate high ground.

OUR VALUES

  • Be the offset. We create asymmetric advantages with creativity and ingenuity.
  • What would it take? We challenge assumptions to deliver ambitious results.
  • It’s the people. Our team is our competitive advantage and we are better together.

YOUR MISSION

We are looking for a technical heavyweight to shape the physical backbone of how we build our products. You think in systems, not just rooms — when you look at a line layout, you don't just ask whether it works today, you ask whether it serves where we're headed. You'll be the force multiplier for our Production Engineering team, pushing toward smarter, leaner infrastructure and layout decisions that buy us flexibility, cost savings, and speed. You thrive in ambiguity: you rarely get every input upfront, but you know how to work internal and external stakeholders to keep progress moving despite the gaps. You think in long horizons too — master planning where engineering programs are best suited to live, and getting ahead of long-lead requirements before they become bottlenecks. And you hold people accountable — external vendors and internal partners alike — to deliver the data and rigor that every program request demands.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Lead the strategic design and build-out of the facilities components of the manufacturing/production pipeline, working hand-in-hand with Production Engineering to determine infrastructure requirements and line design. Navigate ambiguity by partnering with internal and external stakeholders to drive progress even when design inputs are incomplete. Support long-term master planning to determine where engineering programs are best located, getting ahead of long-lead requirements before they constrain the schedule. Challenge and pressure-test layouts against long-term objectives, ensuring programming and design serve where production is headed — not just where it is today. Drive the manufacturing engineering team toward layout and engineering decisions that maximize flexibility, cost savings, throughput, and speed. Hold external vendors — like architects, engineers, contractors — and internal cross-functional partners accountable to providing the data needed to support program requests. Develop, implement, and govern production facility standards that ensure consistency, scalability, throughput, and quality across all sites. Design and deliver production environments that prioritize growth strategy, worker safety, and productivity across all spaces. Own the facilities scope of line build-out projects from concept through commissioning.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • 10+ years of experience in manufacturing or critical infrastructure design
  • Degree in architecture, engineering, or construction
  • Deep technical fluency in production line design, infrastructure requirements, and manufacturing facility build-out
  • Proven ability to navigate ambiguity and drive progress with incomplete information
  • Experience with long-term master planning and managing long-lead requirements
  • Proven ability to evaluate and rethink layouts against long-term operational objectives
  • Track record of driving cost, flexibility, throughput, and speed gains through smart layout and engineering decisions
  • Demonstrated ability to hold external vendors and cross-functional partners accountable to data and deliverables
  • Demonstrated ability to develop and govern facility standards across multiple sites
  • Experience partnering closely with manufacturing or production engineering teams
  • Experience scaling production facilities in a high-growth environment
  • Ability to own projects from concept through commissioning

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

  • Experience designing or delivering secure production environments
  • Professional licensure (e.g., PE, RA)

COMPENSATION

  • Base Salary: $150,000 - $240,000
  • Equity + Benefits including Health, Dental, Vision, HRA/HSA options, PTO and paid holidays, 401K, Parental Leave

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, location, and experience.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Work Location—Successful candidates will be located near Long Beach, CA.

This position will be open until it is successfully filled. To submit your application, please follow the directions below. #LI-Onsite

description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

COMMERCIAL COUNSEL, SUPPLY CHAIN

As a Commercial Counsel on the SpaceX Legal Team, you will enable SpaceX’s procurement of critical goods and services by providing legal review and solutions-based counseling to Supply Chain, Purchasing, Facilities and other cross-functional partners on complex legal and business issues in the United States and internationally.

title: Broista – Hollister, CA
description:
It's fun to work in a company where people truly believe in what they are doing. At Dutch Bros Coffee, we are more than just a coffee company. We are a fun-loving, mind-blowing company that makes a difference one cup at a time.

At Dutch Bros Coffee, we are a fun-loving, mind-blowing company, making a massive difference one cup at a time.

title: Scientist I-II, Analytical Development
description:
About Antheia:
Antheia is the advanced biosynthesis company transforming pharmaceutical manufacturing and innovation for the 21st century. Antheia’s commercially proven technology platform produces high-value pharmaceutical ingredients in a fraction of the time compared to legacy approaches while significantly reducing supply chain risk. The company provides its global pharmaceutical customers with a resilient, efficient supply of critical ingredients at scale, while expanding the innovation frontier for new therapeutic development. Backed by leading investors and recognized by the U.S. government as a priority technology for public health and national and economic security, Antheia is manufacturing the medicines the world needs today while enabling tomorrow’s breakthrough therapeutics.

Working at Antheia:
Our cross-functional team shares a vision for the future: improved pharmaceutical supply chains that can end drug shortages and drive equitable access to essential medicines. As a team, we aim to embody a culture that celebrates diversity, prioritizes knowledge sharing, encourages exploration and ideation, challenges constructively, and supports individuals in their professional and personal journeys. At Antheia, you can expect to be inspired by the science, by your teammates, and by the opportunity we have to bring about change in the pharmaceutical industry.

Who We Are

Antheia is the advanced biosynthesis company transforming pharmaceutical manufacturing and innovation for the 21st century. Antheia’s commercially proven technology platform produces high-value pharmaceutical ingredients in a fraction of the time compared to legacy approaches while significantly reducing supply chain risk. The company provides its global pharmaceutical customers with a resilient, efficient supply of critical ingredients at scale, while expanding the innovation frontier for new therapeutic development. Backed by leading investors and recognized by the U.S. government as a priority technology for public health and national and economic security, Antheia is manufacturing the medicines the world needs today while enabling tomorrow’s breakthrough therapeutics.

As a key member of Analytical Development group, you will be responsible for working closely with biology and fermentation teams to develop, implement and support analytical solutions to guide metabolic engineering and scale-up process by evaluation of metabolites from engineered yeast strains in microtiter plates up to multi-L tank scale. This includes refining and executing analytical operations to handle large sample numbers in timely manner, as well as developing specialized methods across HPLC, UPLC, LC-MS, and GC-MS instruments. A successful candidate will be very organized and detail-oriented, self-driven and possess leadership qualities to deliver high value solutions and processes in fast-paced environment.

Responsibilities

  • Perform analytical method development and optimization for quantification of small molecules using UPLC-UV, LC-MS and GC-MS instruments from sample preparation to data analysis and interpretation
    Collaborate with scientists in biology and fermentation to understand analytical needs, deliver feedback on feasibility, timelines, and resource requirements of their requests, and deliver maximum value by developing appropriate method and process in house or outsourcing to external laboratories.
  • Manage, coach, and mentor a small team of Analytical Chemists, direct daily work and task, conduct performance evaluations, set goals, and provide constructive feedback.
  • Develop and implement processes to quickly and unambiguously address issues with unexpected analytical results, timely troubleshoot and resolve analytical method related errors and give feedback to biology and fermentation teams.
  • Be a subject matter expert for all routine in-house assays, train and guide junior staff in execution of those assays to defined specs in a timely manner.
  • Prioritize work of junior staff between routine analytical operation and method development and optimization activities to minimize sample backlog and achieve development goals, give feedback to senior management if there are resource constraints and collaborate on finding solutions.
  • Perform maintenance and troubleshoot common instrumentation failures and errors.
  • Prepare samples for routine analysis including instrument setup and data analysis
  • Prepare technical reports/SOPs and clearly communicate scientific findings.
  • Adhere to safe laboratory practices.
  • Perform other duties as assigned

Qualifications

  • B.S. with 10+ years of experience or Ph.D. with 2+ years of experience in Analytical Chemistry or related field.
  • Experience with UPLC/UV, LC/MS/MS and GC/MS on fermentation-derived matrices required.
  • Proven track record of successful method development and qualification.
  • Theoretical knowledge of diverse analytical techniques.
  • Motivation and ability to solve complex analytical problems and build effective processes in a startup environment.
  • Experience managing direct reports with proven ability to delegate tasks, motivate staff, and make balanced operational decisions under pressure
  • Experience of collaborative work across multiple teams, building trust, fulfilling requests, giving constructive feedback, resolve conflicts and meeting timelines.
  • Experience working with Agilent software.
  • Experience with Agilent Bravo liquid handling automation and Agilent RapidFire is a plus.

Compensation

$120,000 - $155,000 annual base salary

For full-time employees, Antheia offers a comprehensive total rewards package. Part-time (<30 hours per week) and temporary roles are not eligible for Company sponsored benefits.

  • Comprehensive compensation package, which includes annual bonus potential and equity opportunities

title: Swim Team Head Coach - Seasonal
description:
Atlanta Athletic Club's (AAC) outstanding reputation is based on its unyielding passion for excellence in the quality of services and experiences we offer. We are proud to provide a working environment that embodies our Core Values of Respect, Integrity, Stewardship, and Enthusiasm (RISE).
SWIM TEAM HEAD COACH - SEASONAL
Position Overview

The Head Coach is responsible for leading, developing, and managing all aspects of the swim team program. This position requires a dynamic leader who demonstrates strong communication, organizational, and motivational skills while fostering a positive and competitive environment for student-athletes of all skill levels. The Head Coach will promote sportsmanship, discipline, and teamwork while maintaining the highest standards of safety, professionalism, and integrity.
Primary Responsibilities:

Leadership & Program Management
  • Provide authoritative and inspiring leadership to all swimmers and assistant coaches.
  • Develop and implement a structured training program that emphasizes skill development, conditioning, and performance progression for student ages ranging from 5–18-year-olds.
  • Establish and enforce team rules, expectations, and conduct standards.
  • Manage daily practice sessions, meets, and Saturday clinic programs.
Communication & Collaboration
  • Maintain open, professional communication with athletes, parents, staff, and administration.
  • Collaborate with AAC team and aquatics director to ensure alignment with program goals.
Athlete Development
  • Foster a culture of respect, accountability, and continuous improvement.
  • Mentor athletes in goal setting, sportsmanship, and time management.
  • Evaluate individual performance and provide constructive feedback.
  • Knowledge of stroke technique, training principles, and competitive strategies.
Safety & Compliance
  • Ensure all practices and competitions are conducted safely and in compliance with facility and league regulations.
  • Monitor the physical and emotional well-being of all team members.
  • Ability to motivate and maintain discipline among student-athletes.
  • Demonstrated commitment to promoting sportsmanship, teamwork, and personal growth.
Skills and Abilities:
  • Proven experience in competitive swim coaching with a history of athlete development and program success.
  • Strong leadership, organizational, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Strong communication and customer-service skills with a focus on clarity and professionalism.
  • Highly organized with the ability to manage multiple tasks, deadlines, and seasonal demands.
  • Proficiency with administrative and swim team management systems (Swimtopia, Meet Manager, Excel, or similar tools).
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, member-facing, youth-centered environment.
  • Physical requirements include the ability to lift 50 pounds, remain standing for extended periods, and perform rescues if necessary.
Education and Certifications:
  • Current CPR and First Aid certification (Lifeguard certification preferred).
  • ASA Certification (required or obtained within 30 days)
  • Safety Training for Swim Coaches (STSC) or equivalent (preferred)
Compensation and Benefits:
  • Competitive seasonal salary with an hourly rate of $25 - $30 paid in season and balance paid upon satisfactory completion of swim season.
  • Enjoy a holiday rate of 1.5 times normal pay on Memorial Day, July 4 and Labor Day
  • Complimentary meals are provided in our team member dining room while on duty
  • Celebrate with your family at our annual summer pool party for all team members
Atlanta Athletic Club is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, color, national origin, ethnicity, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, marital status, pregnancy, child birth, or related medical condition, genetic information, physical or mental disability, military service, covered veteran status, or on the basis of any other status protected by applicable federal, state, and/or local law.

title: Claims Internship Summer 2027 - Stevens Point, WI
description:
In this internship, you'll gain hands-on experience and work with a mentor to learn all about the Claims role and network with leadership at social events.

Here at Sentry, we value real work experience for our interns. We offer not only an internship, but an experience for students to get a head start on their careers, early on. With the claim’s internship, you will work with a mentor to learn what claims are and how they play a vital role in the company’s success, as well as how claims are handled. You will also get opportunities to network by attending diverse social events and meeting leadership in multiple areas.

What You’ll Do

Our Claims internship offers opportunities to:

  • Gain hands-on insight into claims negotiations and settlement processes to help reach fair resolutions for customers.

  • Stand by customers during stressful times, guiding them through the claims process with genuine care and understanding.

  • Review policy details to accurately verify coverage and policy limits for current customers.

  • Dive into the details of a loss by gathering facts and reviewing documentation to understand what happened.

  • Maintain clear, thorough records of all investigations, communications, and steps taken throughout the claims process.

What it Takes

To be considered for this position, the following criteria is necessary:

  • Pursuing an undergraduate or associate degree in Business, Insurance, Communication, or a related field

  • Obtain a minimum in-major GPA of 3.00

  • Expected graduation of May 2028

  • Obtain required licensing as needed

  • Sentry does not offer employment in this position to holders of F-1, J-1, and H-1 Visas for the purpose of obtaining practical experience

What we’re looking for

While we appreciate all kinds of backgrounds and personalities, here are a few key traits and skills our team values for this role:

  • Critical thinking: You enjoy solving problems and looking at challenges from different angles.

  • Independent decision-making: You’re comfortable taking initiative and making thoughtful choices on your own.

  • Team collaboration: You’re a natural team player who loves working together toward shared goals.

  • Empathy: You lead with genuine care and understanding for others, especially when they need it most.

  • Organization: You stay organized, efficient, and focused even when juggling a few things at once.

What You’ll Receive

As a Sentry intern, you won’t just be shadowing. You’ll do real, impactful work while growing your career. Here’s a look at what you can expect:

  • Meaningful experience & mentorship: Dive right into a professional corporate setting where you can add value, build your skills, and get direct exposure to company leadership and executives.

  • Flexibility and a complete setup: Enjoy a hybrid schedule—work from home on Mondays and Fridays and collaborate in the office Tuesday through Thursday—plus all the tech you need, including a laptop and monitors.

  • Financial and living support: Benefit from competitive pay, free housing and parking close to our offices, and a meal stipend depending on your location.

  • Connection and community: Build your professional network and make friends through team social events, community involvement, and networking opportunities.

Why Join Sentry?

At Sentry, we believe our people are the heart of our success. We’re proud to be recognized for both our strong growth and the culture we’ve built—recently ranking No. 529 on the 2026 Fortune 1000 (marking our first time in the top 600) and earning spots on Forbes’ lists for America’s Best Midsize Employers and Best Employers for New Grads, as well as Newsweek’s America’s Greatest Workplaces for Women and Diversity. These honors reflect our commitment to your professional satisfaction and growth.

Building on a Legacy

Our future is bright, but it’s anchored in a long history of stability. Since our founding in 1904, we’ve dedicated ourselves to helping businesses protect their futures. That trust has made us one of the largest and most financially stable mutual insurance companies in the U.S. We’re proud to have maintained an A+ rating from A.M. Best, the industry’s leading authority, for over 30 years.

Your Career, Our Community

Whether you’re working at our headquarters in Stevens Point, Wisconsin, or one of our many offices across the country, you’ll find a challenging and rewarding environment. Explore the Our Teams tab on our Career Page to see the diverse career paths we offer, with a focus on ongoing development and professional growth.

Ready to own your future? Join us at Sentry, opportunities await!

title: ICITAP Export Control Subject Matter Expert - East Asia Pacific
description:
Amentum is a premier global services partner supporting critical programs of national significance across defense, security, intelligence, energy, and environment. Amentum draws from a century-old heritage of operational excellence, mission focus, and successful execution underpinned by a strong culture of safety and ethics. Headquartered in Chantilly, VA., Amentum employs more than 50,000 people on all seven continents.

Amentum is supporting the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) in providing specialized training, advisory and mentoring services to host nations under the Criminal Division’s International Criminal Investigative Training and Assistance Program (ICITAP). https://www.justice.gov/criminal-icitap.

ICITAP is a cornerstone of America’s global strategy for combating transnational crime, terrorism, countering trafficking in persons, establishing rule of law and enhancing human rights in developing countries. Amentum is the contract service provider to the DOJ ICITAP and Overseas Prosecutorial Development, Assistance and Training (OPDAT) programs.

Please Note: This is an Independent Contractor position with Amentum, it should not be considered an employment relationship with Amentum.

POSITION SUMMARY:

Amentum is currently seeking qualified candidates to serve as Subject Matter Experts on Export Control. Location: Remote. This position will be responsible for providing deep regulatory knowledge, and mastery over East Asia Pacific export controls. The candidates will be working as ICITAP TCN advisors to strengthen the capacity of East Asia Pacific region and should be capable of performing the required skills and qualifications as stated in the respective job description. The engagement will last approximately (2 years), with an estimated (5-10) foreign assistance events per year.

JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Participate in project kickoff meetings with government stakeholders.
  • Review existing program documentation and policies.
  • Develop a comprehensive project management plan, including schedule and milestones.
  • Collaborate with interagency officials to develop and implement nonproliferation strategies, with emphasis on export controls, cargo security, and customs practices.
  • Prepare strategy documents and related artifacts (e.g., assessments, stakeholder mapping).
  • Plan, organize, and execute 3-5 foreign assistance events per year (workshops, seminars, webinars, conferences, technical consultations).
  • Develop event agendas and coordinate logistics, including international travel as required.
  • Maintain organized records of all project documents, event materials, and communications.
  • Support knowledge sharing and version control in accordance with government IM/KM practices.
  • Prepare project status reports and event after-action reports.
  • Conduct impact assessments to evaluate the effectiveness of events and activities and provide recommendations for continuous improvement.

REQUIRED SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in international relations, public policy, security studies, or a related field (Master’s degree preferred)
  • Minimum 7 years of relevant professional experience in nonproliferation, export controls, customs, border security, or related national security fields
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex, multi-stakeholder projects, including planning, execution, monitoring, and reporting
  • Strong knowledge of U.S. nonproliferation policy and international frameworks related to export controls, cargo security, and customs enforcement
  • Experience working with U.S. government agencies, international organizations, or foreign government counterparts
  • Proven ability to develop and implement strategic plans and translate policy objectives into operational programs
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to produce reports, briefings, and policy documents for senior audiences
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple priorities under tight deadlines
  • Experience delivering training, workshops, or technical assistance programs
  • Ability to travel internationally, including to countries in the East Asia Pacific region

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Master’s degree or higher in a relevant field such as international security, public administration, or law
  • Regional expertise or prior work experience in East Asia and the Pacific
  • Experience designing and evaluating capacity-building or security assistance programs
  • Prior experience working in or with government agencies responsible for border security, trade compliance, or law enforcement
  • Foreign language proficiency relevant to the East Asia Pacific region
  • Experience coordinating inter-agency or international initiatives
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively in cross-cultural environments and build strong international partnerships

Compensation Details:

$66.35/hour

Actual compensation may vary based on factors such as job responsibilities, education, experience, skills, internal equity, market data, applicable collective bargaining agreements, and relevant laws.

Our health and welfare benefits are designed to support you and your priorities. Offerings include:

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance

  • Paid time off and holidays

  • Retirement benefits (including 401(k) matching)

  • Educational reimbursement

  • Parental leave

title: Patient Transporter
description:
Transports all patient populations to and from examinations and treatments. Performs general errands and other routine duties including cleaning equipment, securing supplies, and other tasks as required. Acts as a team member in the delivery of quality patient care. Adheres to unit procedures wherever transport services rendered.

Essential Functions

  • Practicing safe lifting and techniques, transports patients by assisting patients in and out of cars, lifting patients on and off beds, moving patients to and from special services and treatment areas using wheelchairs, gurneys, or moveable beds.

  • Prepares patient for transport and performs passive and active identification to ensure all patients are properly identified before transporting.

  • Transports all patients and equipment to and from testing and procedure areas including inpatient, outpatient, emergency and high risk Intensive Care Unit (ICU).

  • Effectively communicates with medical employees to ensure all required medical supplies and medications are appropriately transported with the patient including the administering of oxygen when required.

  • Responsible for the timely discharge of patients throughout the hospital.

  • Under the direction of medical employees and/or Registered Nurse (RN), assists in providing support in toileting ambulatory patients.

  • Cleans and disinfects equipment according to established policies and procedures. Maintains clean work areas and returns equipment to appropriate department. Communicates malfunctioning equipment/instruments to appropriate department/unit staff.

  • Actively participates in safety initiatives and risk mitigating measures where appropriate and completes all position and unit safety related competencies and requirements on a timely basis.

  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Required

  • Successful completion of three months of on-the-job-training.

  • High school diploma or equivalent

  • BLS (AHA, American Heart Association) or BLS (ARC, American Red Cross) within 90 days of hire.

  • Understands and demonstrates safe lifting and transport techniques.

  • Knows and practices Universal Precautions as appropriate.

  • Demonstrated communication skills to interact with courtesy, tact, empathy, and professionalism in daily interaction with patients, their families, clinical licensed and non-licensed staff, physicians, and management.

  • Ability to understand and follow directions, ability to comply with HIPAA confidentiality requirements.

  • The ability to recognize if the patient is experiencing stress or other issues during transport and immediately seek assistance.

Preferred

  • Experience in patient transportation in an acute hospital environment.

title: Koneistaja
description:
Koneistaja - CNC-sorvaaja ja aarporaaja

Oletko motivoitunut koneistuksen ammattilainen, joka etsii pitkäaikaista työpaikkaa vakaassa ja kehittyvässä työympäristössä? Haemme asiakkaallemme CNC-koneistajia raskaan konepajateollisuuden tehtäviin. Työtehtävistä (2 paikkaa) toinen koostuu raskaiden konepajatuotteiden CNC-sorvauksesta ja toisessa aarporauksesta. Tehtävät ovat monipuolisia, joten työssä tarvitaan ymmärrystä koneiden ohjelmoinnista, teknisten piirustusten lukutaitoa sekä mittausosaamista.

Työtehtävät:

CNC-sorvaaja:

* Raskaiden konepajatuotteiden CNC-koneistus, ohjelmien ajaminen ja muokkaaminen
* Kappaleiden mittaus ja laadunvarmistus
* Teknisten piirustusten tulkinta ja työohjeiden mukainen työskentely

Aarporaaja:

* Isojen kappaleiden aarporaus ja muut koneistustehtävät
* Kappaleiden mittaus ja laadunvarmistus
* Teknisten piirustusten tulkinta ja työohjeiden mukainen työskentely
* Koneiden asetukset sekä ohjelmoinnin ymmärtäminen ja hyödyntäminen työssä

Tarjoamme:

* Pitkäaikaisen työsuhteen vakaassa ja arvostetussa yrityksessä
* Mahdollisuuden kehittyä ammattilaisena ja edetä vaativampiin tehtäviin
* Työyhteisön, joka panostaa työntekijöiden sitouttamiseen ja pitkäjänteiseen yhteistyöhön
* Kilpailukykyisen palkkauksen osaamisen ja kokemuksen mukaan, uran alkuvaiheen osaajalle arviolta 14-17 e/h ja kokeneelle ammattilaiselle arviolta 17-22 e/h.

Työtä tehdään pääasiassa kahdessa vuorossa, mutta tehtävässä edellytetään valmiutta kolmivuorotyöhön.

Odotamme:

* CNC-sorvauksen/aarporauksen hallintaa ja ymmärrystä koneiden ohjelmoinnista
* Teknisten piirustusten lukutaitoa
* Mittausosaamista ja matemaattista hahmotuskykyä
* Huolellista ja vastuullista työotetta
* Sujuvaa suomen kielen taitoa
* Halua sitoutua pitkäaikaiseen työsuhteeseen ja kehittyä ammattilaisena

Kuulostaa hyvältä, mutta miksi hakisin töitä juuri Amikon kautta?

Amiko tarjoaa kaiken tasoisille ammattilaisille laajan valikoiman töitä. Olemme sinulle reilu, luotettava ja joustava työelämän kumppani. Amikolla on hyvä maine työmarkkinoilla. Pyrimme aina etsimään parhaat mahdolliset ratkaisut työllistymisesi tueksi. Amikolaisena saat:

Vähintään TES:in mukaisen palkkauksen-palkkausjärjestelmämme on kannustava, joskus jopa suurempi kuin työllistyessä suoraan yrityksen palkkalistoille.

Laajasti erilaisia työmahdollisuuksia- meillä on kattavat verkostot ja laaja työpaikkavalikoimaniin osa-aikaisia, kokopäiväisiä kuin sesonkitöitä monelta eri alalta. Kun sopiva työ löytyy, monille tarjoutuu myös mahdollisuus siirtyä vakituiseksi työntekijäksi asiakasyritykseen.

Oman yhteyshenkilön ja yksilöllistä työnhakua – Amikolta saat henkilökohtaista palvelua ja oman tutun yhteyshenkilön, johon voit olla suoraan yhteydessä.

Kattavat työterveyspalvelut, normaalin eläkekertymän ja sairausajan palkan sairauden sattuessa – Vaikka teetkin työsi asiakasyrityksessämme, olet amikolainen ja kannamme sinusta vastuun ja huolehdimme eduistasi.

vai kenties jotain ihan uutta urallesi? Autamme myös alanvaihdossa. Räätälöidyt uravalmennukset auttavat päivittämään osaamistasi ja löytämään uuden suunnan urallasi.

Voisiko tässä olla sinulle uusi työpaikka?

Toimimme asiakkaallemme rekrytointikumppanina, käsittelemme saapuvat työhakemukset sekä vastaamme ensimmäisen vaiheen haastatteluista. Jätäthän hakemuksesi pikimmiten tai soita Amikon Ilonalle p. 050 3589561 ja nappaa itsellesi uusi huippuduuni!

Aloitamme haastattelut jo hakuaikana ja täytämme paikan heti sopivien henkilöiden löydyttyä.

Huomioithan, että emme käsittele sähköpostitse vastaanotettuja hakemuksia vaan jätäthän hakemuksen nettisivujemme kautta tietosuojasyistä.

Please note that we do not process applications submitted by e-mail, so please submit your application via our website for privacy and data protection reasons.

title: Program Manager
description:
Work Location: Onsite, STR Bucks - Levittown, PA

Schedule: Tuesday - Saturday 9am-5pm

STR Bucks County is an outpatient mental health and substance use disorder treatment program in Levittown, Pennsylvania, offering partial hospitalization (PHP), intensive outpatient (IOP), and supportive housing for adults navigating substance use disorders, mental health conditions, and co-occurring disorders.

As part of STR Behavioral Health’s comprehensive continuum of care, STR Bucks County provides individualized, evidence-based treatment to support recovery and help clients stay connected to their work, home, and community. Treatment plans are built around each person’s unique needs and goals — because recovery looks different for everyone.

What we offer:

  • Collaborative environment dedicated to clinical excellence
  • Multiple Career Development Pathways
  • Company Supported Continuing Education & Certification
  • Multiple Health Plan Design Options Available
  • Flexible Dental & Vision Plan Options
  • 100% Company Paid EAP Emotional Well-Being Support
  • 100% Company Paid Critical Illness (with health enrollment plan)
  • 100% Company Paid Life & ADD
  • 401K with Company Match
  • Company-Sponsored HSA, FSA, & DSA Tax Savings Accounts
  • Generous Team Member Referral Program
  • Parental Leave

Position Summary
The Program Manager oversees the Behavioral Health Technicians (BHTs) team at a designated facility. Their
responsibilities include training, scheduling, and immediate supervision of the team. Additionally, they collaborate with
the Executive Director to maintain client safety and customer service. The Program Manager also provides support for
both staff and clients through various clinical and administrative activities, with the goal of achieving optimal client
outcomes.


Relationships and Contacts
Within the organization: Maintains frequent and close working relationships with team members throughout all levels
of the facility.


Outside the organization: Initiates and maintains professional therapeutic engagement with clients/families, clinical
providers, referral partners and vendors as needed and directed.


Position Responsibilities
Essential Responsibilities
1. Provides immediate supervision for BHTs in the oversite of clients ensuring client safety.
2. Participates in hiring process, training, coaching, mentoring, and completes annual employee evaluations.
3. Leads meetings for the BHTs team and engages team in performance improvement activities.
4. Collaborates with the Director and represents BHTs team in Treatment Team, Leadership, and other meetings as
required.
5. Understands the organization’s vision and strategic goals.
6. Ensures contract compliance and program quality according to local state and federal laws, as well as best
practices.
7. Ensures that the values and cultural beliefs are taken into account when assisting with the treatment of the
clients.
8. Monitors program goals in alignment with established policies and procedures.
9. Promotes client involvement in the treatment facility; supports clients throughout their treatment journey.
10. Performs routine forms of daily client care while assisting and ensuring timely and effective clinical activities,
charting and orientation completion.
11. Collaborates with the Clinical Director to ensure appropriate emotional support is provided to clients.
12. Communicates pertinent client information to the Clinical team in a timely manner.
13. Maintains timely/clinically appropriate documentation, ensuring BHTs are trained in and adhere to
documentation processes.
14. Assists with the timely completion of administrative duties, including but not limited to checklists, answering
phones, mail distribution, scheduling.
15. Assists with the timely completion of housekeeping duties, including cleaning of facilities (i.e., taking out trash,
loading and unloading dishwasher, laundry, running errands and other duties as assigned).
16. Represents the BHTs team in treatment team meetings, leadership meetings, and other meetings as needed.
17. Conducts tours for clients, family members, students, visitors, as requested.
18. Updates job knowledge by participating in training and educational opportunities.
Program Manager job description p. 2
Revised: 5/30/24
19. Serves as a trainer and mentor to the BHTs, providing coaching for continuous quality improvement.
Additional Responsibilities
1. Functions within the guidelines of the facility’s Code of Ethics and in accordance with corporate compliance.
2. Conducts chart audits following program policy timelines, as requested.
3. Consistently arrives to work on time, rarely missing scheduled shifts, and promptly notifies supervisor when
absent.
4. Demonstrates an ability to adapt to changes in the facility function, management styles, and facility routines.
5. Reads, understands, adheres to, and models all company policy statements on ethics, conduct, and conflict of
interests.
6. Maintains positive attitude and acts as a team player with others on the treatment team.
7. Attends all supervisory trainings within assigned time frames as required by the facility.
8. Performs other duties as assigned.

title: Product Analyst
description:
Turn pharmacy needs into better software!

At Liberty Software, we proudly partner with client pharmacies across the country, helping them support their patients with powerful, user-friendly software. We're excited to grow our team by hiring a Product Analyst who will partner with a Product Owner to evaluate product capabilities and needs, gather and document requirements, design features, and support sprint execution throughout the product development lifecycle.

Please note:

  • This role is based in our Southlake, TX office
  • Liberty Software does not offer employment sponsorship opportunities for this role (e.g., H-1B, OPT, or other work visa status)

What You’ll Do:

  • Gather, clarify, and document business and functional requirements from stakeholders across the organization
  • Write clear, well-structured user stories with defined acceptance criteria
  • Translate business needs into detailed specifications, functional designs, and product workflows
  • Collaborate with development, QA, and cross-functional teams throughout the design process
  • Assist in sprint planning and agile ceremonies to ensure timely delivery of product features
  • Support user acceptance testing by validating that delivered features meet documented requirements
  • Support beta customer programs by capturing feedback and organizing it into actionable items
  • Analyze product data and usage metrics to identify gaps and recommend improvements
  • Present findings and recommendations to product management and development teams

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Computer Science, information Systems, or related field preferred
  • 2 (two) or more years in a product, business analysis, or pharmacy operations role; prior product analyst experience is preferred; relevant software or pharmacy industry experience will also be considered
  • Familiarity with pharmacy software and healthcare systems is highly desirable
  • Retail pharmacy experience as a technician or pharmacist is a strong plus
  • Strong analytical skills with excellent attention to detail
  • Proficiency with excel and comfort working with date; SQL experience is a strong plus
  • Understanding of agile development methodologies and software development processes, including experience writing user stories and acceptance criteria
  • Experience with agile tools like Jira or similar platforms
  • Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to document complex information clearly
  • Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to collaborate across departments

title: Munitions Handler
description:
Amentum is seeking a Munitions Handler to join our team in Hawthorne, Nevada to support the Hawthorne Army Depot. The Munitions Handler assists with a variety of warehousing and demilitarization duties involving stock movement, inventory, and disassembly/destruction of munitions within controlled environments.

Must be able to obtain and maintain a Secret US Government Clearance. Note: US Citizenship is required to obtain a Secret Clearance. ​

Typical Responsibilities Include:

  • Performs warehousing duties involving movement of ordnance items or components into/out of storage facilities, physical inventory, storage arrangement, accessibility, inspect, loading, and packaging.

  • Processes may be manual, technical, and mechanically assisted within the storage, receipt, shipment, inspection, of explosive ordnance items or components.

  • Perform destruction and demilitarization of ammunition and explosive components.

  • Operate automated systems within a munitions demilitarization process.

  • Follow all pertinent local, state, and federal compliance documents and procedures.

description:

Company: Novus Clinic
