title: Low Yield Analysis Engineer on Shift
description:
Job Details:

Job Description:

APTD LYA is a Foundry Labs Network organization that supports back-end package assembly and wafer level assembly sort and test fails to help root cause yield loss and in-line failures. In this electrical-characterization hybrid role, the engineer on shift will be responsible for technical functions such as design, test, checkout, modifications, and characterization of wafer level assembly technologies. Engineers on back or front of week shift schedules will help bridge support between engineering technicians, as well as shift 1 engineers and module partners, yield support, integration and both internal and external customers in a collaborative environment. As an LYA Engineer, you will set priorities for the platform/project, get results across boundaries, and ensure an inclusive work environment. In this role, engineers can expect to work with a team of engineers and engineering technicians to conduct various analyses and engineering tests to provide platforms with root cause determination of in-line electrical failures and perform defect and/or process characterization in support of identifying key mechanisms that contribute to root cause identification. Your main responsibilities include, but are not limited to: - Working across team boundaries to achieve strategic objectives and meet program deliverables. - Understand program milestones and schedules then translate into team objectives and drive execution. - Interface with a wide variety of internal teams, as well as external suppliers to improve yield and drive innovation. - Project management, package design and/or development and sustaining support for integrated circuit or semiconductor assemblies, as well as various other electronic components and/or completed units. - Conduct hands-on lab work, define data acquisition strategy and data analysis plan, and recommend corrective actions and/or fixes to internal customers. - Develop failure analysis innovative techniques, BKMs, and/or approaches to accelerate failure identification and mechanism understanding. - Provide consultation concerning packaging and/or assembly problems and improvements in the manufacturing process. - Respond to customers' requests or events as they occur. - Candidate should be capable of working effectively across organizational boundaries. - Candidate must exhibit the following traits/skills: Work with ambiguity and flexibility with respect to job roles and working hours, have strong analytical and problem-solving skills, and possess robust communication and presentation skills. This role is lab-based and on-site required.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Experience listed below would be obtained through schoolwork and/or classes and/or project work and/or internships and/or military training and/or work experience. Minimum Qualifications: Must possess a Bachelor's Degree with at least 2 years of experience or Master's Degree in Materials Science and Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or Chemistry and Physics or related field. Preferred Qualifications: • Prior experience working in a lab environment. • Experience with destructive and optical analysis techniques such as manual cross-sectioning and delayering, SEM, x-ray, microscopy, CSAM, ion milling, TEM and FIB • Experience performing electrical fault isolation and failure analysis on product and TV through the use of hand probe, curve trace, auto probing, TDR, EOTPR, EBAC, RIDR, and/or ELITE. • Experience with chemical compositional analysis techniques such as EDX. AFM, FTIR, Raman, and diffraction techniques such as XRD and EBSD. • Knowledge of package or die mapping software EX: Mentor Graphics, SysNav/CadNav, FIELD and expertise in SQL scripting and basic statistical analysis tools such as JMP are a plus. • Ability to communicate findings verbally and through reports to yield engineers, LYA analysts, and other customers. • Ability to work in a collaborative manner with a variety of different individuals in a fast paced, technical environment. • Ability to work effectively in an ambiguous environment where changing priorities and the norm.

title: Senior Engineering Technical Program Manager - Jira Administration
description:
Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human

Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.

This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.

Role Overview

As the Okta Research & Design (ORD) Jira Owner & Administrator, nested within the Technical Program Management (TPM) organization, you will define and execute the strategy for how ORD plans, tracks, and reports on engineering work within the full toolchain of Atlassian Jira, Jira Advanced Roadmaps (Plans), Confluence, Rovo, and AI integrations. In this role, you act as a critical bridge between product & technical leadership, agile teams, and cross-functional business units — translating methodology, best practices, and process frameworks into practical workflow improvements that accelerate delivery and reduce manual overhead for a 1,000+ person engineering, product, and design organization.

By optimizing tooling configurations, automating reporting, and eliminating fragmented management processes, you will directly accelerate ORD’s developer velocity and strengthen operational efficiency.

Core Responsibilities

1. Platform Ownership & Strategic Tooling Direction

  • Strategic Vision: Define, implement, govern an AI-led strategy for utilizing Jira for product planning, tracking, and reporting tooling that supports end-to-end portfolio tracking from high-level corporate objectives down to sprint-level stories.
  • E2E Ecosystem Management: Complete ORD ownership of the toolchain (Jira, Jira advanced Roadmaps, AI integrations, Confluence), overseeing architecture, schema updates, workflow management, screen/notification schemes, custom fields, permission sets, and AI integrations.
  • Scale and Automation: Design a highly automated, self-service model that easily scales to accommodate organizational growth in user volume and environmental complexity.
  • AI Tool Integration: Lead evaluation, piloting, and rollout of AI-powered tooling (e.g., Atlassian Rovo, Claude for Jira, AI Companion) to automate ticket triage, sprint planning suggestions, and status summarization.

2. Engineering Process Optimization & Standardization

  • PDLC Alignment: Partner closely with Product Management, Engineering, Quality Assurance, and Security to align tool mechanics with the company's release cadences, secure SDLC requirements, and change control policies.
  • Workflow Design: Standardize Jira workflows to track key engineering pillars uniformly (e.g., New Feature Development, Architecture Improvements, and Run-the-Business/KTLO operations).
  • Eliminate Tool Fragmentation: Actively lead efforts to migrate teams away from disjointed standalone tracking sheets and custom scripts into Jira to create a single, synchronized source of truth.

3. Data Governance & Analytics Enablement

  • Source of Truth Data: Ensure data integrity within Jira to allow executive leadership to accurately assess resource allocation, identify horizontal dependencies, map organizational priorities, and make informed business investment decisions.
  • Metrics Reporting: Oversee configurations for integrated reporting engines (such as Faros.ai) to surface real-time visibility into engineering productivity metrics, cycle time, lead time, pipeline health, and bottleneck identification.
  • Change Control & Risk Management: Serve as a core member of the Jira Change Control Board (CCB), assessing the risk levels (Low, Medium, High) of configuration requests to protect the functionality of critical engineering dashboards and tracking filters.

4. Direct Support & Enablement Packages

  • User Enablement: Create intuitive, scalable enablement packages, documentation, and training guides to ensure seamless platform onboarding for new and existing Oktanauts.
  • Ongoing Administration: Act as an independent administrator managing day-to-day configuration requests, custom JQL filtering, role/privilege assignments, and automation rules.
  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Collaborate deeply with internal customers—Developers, Scrum Masters, Engineering Managers, Design Leads, and Product Leads—to capture gaps and build creative process improvements.

Qualifications & Profile

Minimum Qualifications

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Business Technology, or a related field; or equivalent practical experience.
  • Atlassian Expertise: Proven, hands-on experience in Advanced Jira and Confluence Administration within an enterprise-scale engineering ecosystem (supporting 500+ users).
  • Technical Languages: Essential proficiency with Jira Query Language (JQL), basic SQL, or equivalent database queries.
  • AI Proficiency: Hands-on experience integrating AI tools (e.g., Claude, Gemini, Atlassian Rovo, GitHub Copilot) into product development workflows, with a demonstrated ability to evaluate, pilot, and scale AI capabilities across engineering teams.
  • Agile Methodology: Thorough understanding of agile/lean development, Scrum frameworks, sprint execution ceremonies, and SAFe/Portfolio-level planning models.
  • PDLC & SDLC Knowledge: Deep conceptual awareness of modern software engineering practices, release management trains, CI/CD pipelines, and infrastructure deployment models.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Advanced Tools: Deep experience leveraging Jira Service Management, Jira Advanced Roadmaps (Plans), and metrics platforms like Faros.ai.
  • Scripting & Automation: Strong willingness or ability to extend native Atlassian functionality through scripting, macros, and API automations.
  • Analytical Rigor: Excellent critical thinking and advanced troubleshooting capabilities using application logs and configuration event logs.
  • Communication: Stellar written and verbal communication skills; a proven track record of synthesizing dense technical conditions into clear executAI Workflow Design: Experience designing AI-augmented workflows — such as automated ticket enrichment, AI-driven sprint retrospectives, or LLM-assisted reporting — that reduce manual TPM overhead.

title: Lead Avionics Integration & Test Engineer (Starshield)
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

LEAD AVIONICS INTEGRATION & TEST ENGINEER (STARSHIELD PRODUCTION)

Starshield leverages SpaceX’s Starlink technology and launch capability to support national security efforts. While Starlink is designed for consumer and commercial use, Starshield is designed for government use, with an initial focus on earth observation, communications, and hosted payloads.

In this role, you will lead a portion of the team responsible for designing, developing, troubleshooting, and maintaining the hardware test systems used to develop, produce and qualify our satellites. As the lead, you would cultivate your direct reports to develop electrical, RF, and software solutions that quickly and thoroughly validate each component of satellite hardware. Our engineers thrive in this multidisciplinary environment with ever-changing needs as we strive to make a significant contribution to the capabilities of our nation for the decades to come.

Our development timelines are quick, and you and your team will need to rigorously explore solutions for previously unsolved or unknown problems. Every day we push the limits of what is possible through innovation, determination, and teamwork to drive the mission to success.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Provide strong technical leadership with a focus on continuous improvement.
  • Manage projects and delegate responsibilities effectively to complete work on time.
  • Determine team goals to effectively implement testing solutions.
  • Develop and enforce processes to standardize test system deliverable expectations.
  • Develop highly reliable autonomous test systems.
  • Own all aspects of test development, including requirements evaluation, system development, subsystem testing, and factory integration.
  • Collaborate with teams, lead projects, and continuously drive improvement in hardware testing.
  • Create modular, reusable software in Python to automate manufacturing processes and tests.
  • Collaborate directly with the design and manufacturing engineers to validate flight hardware.
  • Actively maintain tests that support rapid design iteration of flight hardware and software.
  • Develop test infrastructure that enables scaling to large numbers of devices under test.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, physics or another engineering discipline.
  • 2+ years of professional experience in testing or hardware development.
  • 1+ years of leadership experience leading teams, projects or people.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • 5+ years of professional design and/or hands-on manufacturing experience.
  • 3+ years of prior leadership experience leading teams, projects or people.
  • Master's degree in engineering or related discipline.
  • Experience leading a team of diverse individuals.
  • Excellent communication and organizational skills both written and verbal.
  • Thorough knowledge of electrical systems.
  • Thorough knowledge of computer architecture and networks.
  • Creative approach to problem solving, exceptional analytical skills and engineering fundamentals.
  • Experience developing, debugging, and deploying electrical test systems that have been used in real-world applications/projects.
  • Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs and requirements.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Must be available to work extended hours as needed to support mission-critical objectives.
  • An active clearance may provide the opportunity for you to work on sensitive SpaceX missions; if so, you will be subject to pre-employment drug and random drug and alcohol testing.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:
$140,000.00 - $230,000.00

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.

Those with an active clearance will receive a 10% differential, up to an additional $20,000 annually, once officially briefed into a classified program.

A World Class Clearing Organization

As a Systemically Important Financial Market Utility (SIFMU), OCC operates under the jurisdiction of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), and the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. description:
CRA II

Syneos Health® is a leading fully-integrated life sciences services organization built to accelerate customer success. We partner with innovators at every point across the drug development and commercialization continuum, helping them navigate complexity, anticipate change and accelerate progress.

Our Clinical Solutions team members act with a drug development mindset, applying their years of experience and deep expertise to truly understand customer needs and represent those in the solutions we shape.

Whether you join us in a Functional Service Provider partnership or a Full-Service environment, you’ll collaborate with passionate problem solvers, innovating as a team to help our customers achieve their goals. We are agile and driven to deliver – for one another, our customers, and, most importantly, for those in need.

Discover what your 25,000 future colleagues already know:

Why Syneos Health
• We are passionate about developing our people, through career development and progression; supportive and engaged line management; technical and therapeutic area training; peer recognition and total rewards program.
• We are committed to building an inclusive culture – where you can authentically be yourself. Central to this is our purpose – Driven to Deliver – which captures the passion of our colleagues to show up each day and shape solutions that have the ability to dramatically impact someone’s life.
• We are continuously building the company we all want to work for and our customers want to work with. Why? Because we know that when we bring together smart colleagues from across the world, we can shape the future of healthcare, driving impact for customers and defining the pace of patient progress.

Job Responsibilities

  • Performs site qualification, site initiation, interim monitoring, site management activities and close-out visits (performed on-site or remotely) ensuring regulatory, ICH-GCP and/or Good Pharmacoepidemiology Practice (GPP) and protocol compliance. Uses judgment and experience to evaluate overall performance of site and site staff and to provide recommendations regarding site-specific actions; immediately communicates/escalates serious issues to the project team and develops action plans. Maintains a working knowledge of ICH/GCP Guidelines or other applicable guidance, relevant regulations, and company SOPs/processes.
  • Verifies the process of obtaining informed consent has been adequately performed and documented for each subject/patient, as required/appropriate. Demonstrates diligence in protecting the confidentiality of each subject/patient. Assesses factors that might affect subject/patient’s safety and clinical data integrity at an investigator/physician site such as protocol deviation/violations and pharmacovigilance issues.
  • Per the Clinical Monitoring/Site Management Plan (CMP/SMP): Assesses site processes. Conducts Source Document Review of appropriate site source documents and medical records. Verifies required clinical data entered in the case report form (CRF) is accurate and complete. Applies query resolution techniques remotely and on site, and provides guidance to site staff as necessary, driving query resolution to closure within agreed timelines. Utilizes available hardware and software to support the effective conduct of the clinical study data review and capture. Verifies site compliance with electronic data capture requirements.
  • May perform investigational product (IP) inventory, reconciliation and reviews storage and security. Verifies the IP has been dispensed and administered to subjects/patients according to the protocol. Verifies issues or risks associated with blinded or randomized information related to IP. Applies knowledge of GCP/local regulations and organizational procedures to ensure IP is appropriately (re)labelled, imported and released/returned.
  • Routinely reviews the Investigator Site File (ISF) for accuracy, timeliness and completeness. Reconciles contents of the ISF with the Trial Master File (TMF). Ensures the investigator/physician site is aware of the requirement of archiving essential documents in accordance with local guidelines and regulations.
  • Documents activities via confirmation letters, follow-up letters, trip reports, communication logs, and other required project documents as per SOPs and Clinical Monitoring Plan/Site Management Plan. Supports subject/patient recruitment, retention and awareness strategies. Enters data into tracking systems as required to track all observations, ongoing status and assigned action items to resolution.
  • For assigned activities, understands project scope, budgets, and timelines; manages site-level activities / communication to ensure project objectives, deliverables and timelines are met. Must be able to quickly adapt to changing priorities to achieve goals / targets.
  • May act as primary liaison with study site personnel, or in collaboration with Central Monitoring Associate. Ensures all assigned sites and project-specific site team members are trained and compliant with applicable requirements
  • Prepares for and attends Investigator Meetings and/or sponsor face to face meetings. Participates in global clinical monitoring/project staff meetings (inclusive of Sponsor representation, as applicable) and attends clinical training sessions according to the project specific requirements.
  • Provides guidance at the site and project level towards audit readiness standards and supports preparation for audit and required follow-up actions.
  • Maintains a working knowledge of ICH/GCP Guidelines or other applicable guidance, relevant regulations, and company SOPs/processes; completes assigned training as required. For Real World Late Phase, the CRA II will use the business card title of Site Management Associate II. Additional responsibilities include:Site support throughout the study lifecycle from site identification through close-out. Knowledge of local requirements for real world late phase study designs.Chart abstraction activities and data collection
    Collaboration with Sponsor affiliates, medical science liaisons and local country staff. The SMA II may be requested to train junior staff. Identify and communicate out of scope activities to Lead CRA/Project Manager. Proactively suggest potential sites based on local knowledge of treatment patterns, patient advocacy and Health Care Provider (HCP) associations.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or RN in a related field or equivalent combination of education, training and experience
  • Knowledge of Good Clinical Practice/ICH Guidelines and other applicable regulatory requirements
  • Must demonstrate good computer skills and be able to embrace new technologies
  • Excellent communication, presentation and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to manage required travel of up to 75% on a regular basis
  • US ONLY: As part of your employment with Syneos Health, you may be deployed to Sites that require certain medical and other personal information to gain facility access. Pursuant to our Employee Privacy Notice, Syneos Health can provide the Sites with the information necessary for you to gain such access. Further, a Site may ask you for additional information beyond that which Syneos Health has in its possession. You are required to comply with any such Site requests as a condition of your employment with Syneos Health. Please note that failure to provide requested information may result in a Site barring you from entry, which could put your ongoing employment at risk.

Get to know Syneos Health


Over the past 5 years, we have worked with 94% of all Novel FDA Approved Drugs, 95% of EMA Authorized Products and over 200 Studies across 73,000 Sites and 675,000+ Trial patients.

No matter what your role is, you’ll take the initiative and challenge the status quo with us in a highly competitive and ever-changing environment. Learn more about Syneos Health.

description:
Do you want your voice heard and your actions to count?

Discover your opportunity with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), one of the world’s leading financial groups. Across the globe, we’re 150,000 colleagues, striving to make a difference for every client, organization, and community we serve. We stand for our values, building long-term relationships, serving society, and fostering shared and sustainable growth for a better world.

With a vision to be the world’s most trusted financial group, it’s part of our culture to put people first, listen to new and diverse ideas and collaborate toward greater innovation, speed and agility. This means investing in talent, technologies, and tools that empower you to own your career.

Join MUFG, where being inspired is expected and making a meaningful impact is rewarded.

A leading global financial institution is seeking a Vice President to join their Debt Capital Markets team in Singapore. This role offers you the opportunity to play a pivotal part in helping clients access global debt markets, while supporting senior originators and contributing to a sustainable, client-focused business across the region. You will be empowered to develop value-added relationships with key clients, work closely with relationship managers, and deliver high-quality support and product interface regarding capital markets financing opportunities. The organisation is committed to fostering an inclusive environment where your expertise is valued, and you are encouraged to collaborate across teams for both personal and professional growth. With flexible working opportunities and ongoing training, this position provides a platform for you to expand your network, enhance your skills, and make a meaningful impact within a supportive leadership structure.

  • Play a central role in origination, structuring, and execution of debt transactions for local, regional, and global capital markets, ensuring smooth deal processes from mandate to closing.

  • Build direct client relationships with a capital markets focus by providing high-quality support and product interface on financing opportunities across multiple debt products and currencies.

  • Benefit from flexible working arrangements, continuous training opportunities, and a knowledgeable team that values collaboration, inclusivity, and growth leadership.

What you'll do:

As Vice President, Debt Capital Markets based in Singapore, you will be responsible for driving origination efforts across the region by developing sustainable client relationships focused on flow-oriented primary market business. Your day-to-day activities will involve collaborating closely with relationship managers to provide comprehensive support on capital markets financing opportunities spanning multiple debt products and currencies. You will take ownership of structuring and executing complex debt transactions for issuance into diverse capital markets while managing all aspects of deal execution from due diligence through settlement. By partnering with distribution teams and other group entities globally, you will help deliver innovative solutions tailored to client needs. iHeartMedia is seeking a Multiplatform Producer-Board Operator to produce and distribute compelling Spanish-language content across digital and social platforms, podcasts, television/video and broadcast radio.

Digital content production will be a primary focus of this role. The ideal candidate is a strong multimedia producer with solid editorial judgment, live production experience and the ability to work closely with on-air talent and Programming to develop content from concept and preparation through live execution, editing, publishing and distribution.

• Strong audio and video editing skills and proficiency with professional digital content creation and production tools.

• Experience creating, editing, packaging and publishing short-form and long-form video for major social media and digital platforms.

• Experience producing, editing, packaging and distributing podcasts and other on-demand content.

• Strong Spanish-language writing and copywriting skills for social posts, headlines, descriptions, articles and other digital content.

• Ability to create or adapt graphics, photos and visual assets for digital and social use.

• Strong understanding of how content should be produced and packaged differently for television/video, social media, web, podcasts and broadcast radio.

• Strong editorial judgment and ability to identify timely, relevant and engaging content while maintaining accuracy and appropriate context.

• Experience with broadcast consoles and radio production workflows preferred.

• Ability to work quickly and accurately in live production and fast-moving digital environments and adapt when content, timing or priorities change.

title: Clinician II

location: ICS Offices - Building C - Berlin, VT 05602
description:
Access Clinician

The Adult Access Clinician/Case Manager is a full-time position providing assessment, case management, and brief psychotherapy to adults in crisis. Core duties include providing immediate follow-up to crisis needs, conducting assessments to determine recommended treatments, delivering brief psychotherapy, providing crisis consultation to treatment providers, and handling discharge planning for adults in acute care facilities. Additionally, the role is responsible for coordinating referrals to longer-term providers, providing case management in collaboration with WCMHS programs and other Washington County agencies, maintaining client case records, and attending weekly individual supervision, group supervision, and staff meetings.

This position impacts the agency and the community by providing rapid, mobile crisis intervention and care coordination for adults in acute distress. By working directly in home and field-based environments and collaborating across Emergency/Urgent Programs, Outpatient, CRT, Vermont psychiatric programs, and local community agencies, the role ensures continuity of care, facilitates safe transitions from acute care facilities, and improves access to appropriate longer-term support systems.

Summary of Responsibilities

  • Provide immediate crisis follow-up, assessment, case management, and brief psychotherapy to adults in crisis.
  • Coordinate client care, referrals to longer-term service providers, and discharge planning for adults in acute care facilities.
  • Deliver crisis consultation to treatment providers and collaborate with WCMHS programs and Washington County agencies.
  • Create and participate in treatment team meetings, client advocacy, and behavior management consultations.
  • Maintain complete and timely case records for the population served in accordance with agency paperwork deadlines.
  • Attend required weekly individual supervision, group supervision, and staff meetings.

Compensation and Benefits

The starting pay range for this position is $63,315 to $66,530 annualized.

WCMHS provides a comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, vision, and retirement contribution matching. Our industry-leading paid time off package includes 12.5 flexible holidays and 12 days each of sick vacation days accumulated in year one of employment.

title: Data Engineer II (Restaurant AI CoPilot)
description:
This hybrid role requires working in the office two days per week.

With millions of diners, 70,000+ restaurant partners and 25+ years of experience, OpenTable, part of Booking Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: BKNG), is an industry leader with a passion for helping restaurants thrive. Our world-class technology empowers restaurants to focus on what matters most – their team, their guests, and their bottom line – while enabling diners to discover and book the perfect restaurant for every occasion.

Every employee at OpenTable has a tangible impact on what we do and how we do it. You’ll also be part of a global team and its portfolio of metasearch brands. Hospitality is all about taking care of others, and it defines our culture.

About this Role

As a Data Engineer on the Data Science team at OpenTable, you will design, build, and maintain robust data solutions that power diner features, partner integrations, and advanced AI initiatives. You will work closely with cross-functional teams including Product Managers, Business Intelligence Analysts, Infrastructure SREs, and Product Engineers to deliver scalable data products. Joining a agile, high-impact team, you will leverage OpenTable's vast data ecosystem to drive key business decisions and enhance user experiences globally

Responsibilities

  • Design, test, deploy, and maintain scalable batch and streaming data pipelines to deliver reliable data to internal and external customers
  • Collaborate with Product Managers, Business Intelligence Analysts, SREs, and Product Engineers to architect and govern production data services
  • Build data pipelines providing actionable insights to restaurants regarding guest behaviour, revenue, and operational efficiency
  • Develop and maintain data integrations with external partners to support critical business partnerships and data exchange
  • Power diner analytics and machine learning work streams for Sales, Marketing, and AI initiatives, including generative AI content summarization
  • Monitor and optimize production systems to ensure high performance, data availability, and system integrity

Minimum Qualifications

  • Demonstrated professional experience in data engineering principles, data architecture, and software design
  • Proven track record of building, testing, deploying, monitoring, and maintaining production data systems
  • Proficiency in Python, SQL, and at least one strongly typed language (such as Java)
  • Experience constructing scalable batch and streaming data pipelines
  • Experience working in cross-functional environments and collaborating with product and technical stakeholders

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with data engineering stack components such as PySpark, Databricks, Snowflake, Airflow, Kubernetes, and AWS.
  • Knowledge or experience in Machine Learning development (e.g., NLP, LLMs, RAG, recommendations, or MLOps).
  • Familiarity with containerization, orchestration, and monitoring tools like Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Prometheus, or Grafana.
  • Familiarity with data storage and infrastructure solutions such as Kafka, Snowflake, Delta Lake, or vector/NoSQL databases.
  • Understanding of A/B testing best practices and data-driven product evaluation.

Benefits and Perks

  • Generous paid vacation + time off for your birthday
  • Work from (almost) anywhere for up to 20 days per year
  • Focus on mental health and well-being:
    • Company-paid therapy sessions through SpringHealth
    • Company-paid subscription to Headspace
    • Annual company-wide week off a year - the whole team fully recharges (and returns without a pile-up of work!)
  • Paid parental leave
  • Paid volunteer time
  • Focus on your career growth:
    • Development Dollars
    • Leadership development
    • Access to thousands of on-demand e-learnings
  • Travel Discounts
  • Employee Resource Groups
  • 20 days of paid time off
  • Private health and dental insurance
  • Life and Disability insurance

The best connections happen face-to-face, whether you’re sitting down to dinner or having coffee with a coworker. That’s why OpenTable has adopted a hybrid workplace model. This role aligns with that approach, with an expectation of coming into the office two days a week—giving employees the best of both worlds: in-person collaboration and flexibility.

The expected range of compensation for this position based in Toronto, Canada, including commission and/or bonuses is $120,000 - $130,000 CAD. There are a variety of factors that go into determining a compensation range, including but not limited to external market benchmark data, geographic location, and years of experience sought/required.

We offer a competitive base salary and benefits including: health benefits; flexible spending account; retirement benefits; life insurance; paid time off (including PTO, paid sick leave, medical leave, bereavement leave, floating holidays and paid holidays); and parental leave benefits. This role is eligible to be considered for an annual bonus and equity grant.

Work Environment & Flexibility

At OpenTable, we pride ourselves on fostering a global and dynamic work environment. As a team member with us, you will benefit from a schedule tailored to accommodate a global workforce operating across multiple time zones. While the majority of your responsibilities may align with conventional business hours, there will be instances where you are expected to manage communications - via calls, Slack messages, or emails - outside of regular working hours to effectively collaborate with international colleagues, respond to restaurant partners, and/or address urgent matters. OpenTable will always abide by and consider local laws and regulations.

Inclusion

We’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels they belong and can thrive. We know the best ideas come when we bring different voices to the table, so we're building a team as dynamic as the diners and restaurants we serve—and fostering a culture where everyone feels welcome to be themselves.

If you need accommodations during the application or interview process, or on the job, we’re here to support you. Please reach out to your recruiter to request any accommodations.

title: Process Lead (UPK)
description:

Also, will ensure that the different types of machinery will be in optimal condition, setting up, adjusting, and troubleshooting to have an efficient quality production.

  • Ensure the elaboration of samples for new products, validations and participate in the new implementation process.
  • Monitor and evaluate production processes to identify opportunities for improvement in efficiency, quality, and cost-effectiveness.
  • Conduct other duties as assigned by management.

  • Dependable and Punctual.

  • Basic math and measuring ability.
  • Analytic abilities.
  • Basic abilities using computers or electronic devices.

  • Ability to be organized, multitask and keep up in a fast-paced environment.

title: Lead Infrastructure Engineer (Exchange, Entra, Intune & Microsoft 365)
description:
We are looking for a Lead Infrastructure Engineer to join our Infrastructure Engineering team. This is an exciting opportunity to help design, operate, and evolve enterprise-scale Microsoft 365 and end-user computing platforms, including Exchange Online, Entra ID, Active Directory, Intune, SCCM/MECM, endpoint management, and collaboration services. We would love to speak with you if you have deep hands-on experience engineering complex Microsoft environments and serving as a senior escalation point for identity, messaging, endpoint, and workplace technology platforms.

About You – experience, education, skills, and accomplishments

  • 10+ years of experience supporting, engineering, and operating enterprise Microsoft infrastructure environments.
  • Extensive hands-on experience with Microsoft 365, Exchange Online, Hybrid Exchange, Entra ID, Active Directory, Intune, SCCM/MECM, Microsoft Teams, SharePoint Online, and OneDrive for Business.
  • Experience designing, troubleshooting, and supporting complex Microsoft 365 hybrid environments.
  • Strong understanding of directory services, identity architecture, authentication protocols, federation, SSO, MFA, Conditional Access, and Zero Trust principles.
  • Proven experience managing large-scale endpoint estates, including Windows 10/11, Autopilot, application deployment, patch management, compliance, and device lifecycle management.
  • Expert-level PowerShell scripting and automation skills, with experience using Microsoft Graph or modern infrastructure management techniques.
  • Experience resolving enterprise-wide outages, conducting root cause analysis, and improving operational stability for critical services.
  • Strong understanding of Microsoft licensing, service architecture, security controls, compliance requirements, and operational best practices.

It would be great if you also have . . .

  • Experience with Microsoft Purview, Information Protection, DLP, eDiscovery, and Records Management.
  • Experience with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Defender for Identity, and Defender for Office 365.
  • Experience leading Microsoft 365 tenant-to-tenant migrations, M&A activities, divestitures, or large-scale carve-outs.
  • Familiarity with JAMF, Apple device management, and cross-platform endpoint management.
  • Experience with Azure infrastructure, automation frameworks, Infrastructure as Code, and Microsoft Graph API development.
  • Relevant Microsoft certifications, such as Microsoft 365 Enterprise Administrator Expert, Identity and Access Administrator, Messaging Administrator, Endpoint Administrator, or Azure Administrator.

What will you be doing in this role?

  • Serve as the senior technical authority and Tier 3 escalation point for complex Microsoft infrastructure, identity, messaging, and endpoint management issues.
  • Own the architecture, engineering, and lifecycle management of Microsoft 365 services, including Exchange Online, Entra ID, Teams, SharePoint Online, OneDrive, and Purview.
  • Lead the design and operation of hybrid identity environments integrating Active Directory, Entra ID, federation services, and directory synchronization platforms.
  • Manage enterprise messaging platforms, including Exchange Online, hybrid Exchange deployments, mail routing, transport, compliance, retention, migration, and messaging security.
  • Architect and support enterprise endpoint management capabilities across Intune, SCCM/MECM, Autopilot, device compliance, patch management, and application deployment.
  • Drive automation and operational efficiency through PowerShell, Microsoft Graph, and modern infrastructure management techniques.
  • Partner with Security teams to implement and maintain identity governance, conditional access, privileged access management, DLP, retention, and compliance controls.
  • Support Microsoft 365 tenant optimization, roadmap planning, service modernization, cloud transformation initiatives, and large-scale platform migrations.

About the Team

The Infrastructure Engineering team supports the platforms and services that enable secure, scalable, and modern ways of working across the enterprise. This role will partner closely with Security, IT Operations, Workplace Technology, and business stakeholders to deliver reliable Microsoft 365, identity, messaging, collaboration, and endpoint services.

Hours of Work

This is a full-time position, primarily working core business hours in your time zone, with flexibility to adjust to various global time zones as needed. Work location and hybrid expectations should be confirmed based on the approved requisition details.

¡Impulsa tu carrera y ayuda a crear la próxima generación de vehículos en General Motors!

En el Toluca Regional Engineering Center (TREC) buscamos estudiantes de ingeniería que quieran desarrollar experiencia práctica en el mundo automotriz, participando en proyectos que impactan directamente el desempeño, la calidad y la eficiencia de los vehículos de General Motors.

Trabajarás junto a ingenieros especializados en CAE (Computer-Aided Engineering) y CFD (Computational Fluid Dynamics), contribuyendo al desarrollo y validación virtual de sistemas automotrices mediante herramientas de simulación de clase mundial.

Como parte de los equipos de CAE Thermal, CAE Interiors y CFD Air Handling, participarás en actividades como:

✅ Análisis de esfuerzos y deformaciones (FEA)

Ideal conocimientos de algun lenguaje de programacion como Python, Java, MatlLab, ANSYS, Abaqus, HyperWorks, OptiStruct, LS-DYNA, Nastran, Simcenter, COMSOL Multiphysics, Simulink.

title: HSE Officer
description:
APM Terminals

At APM Terminals, a global leader in port and terminal operations, we enable global trade and drive sustainable growth. What drives us forward is a mindset of always improving, observing how work happens, identifying what creates value, and removing what gets in the way. We constantly look for smarter, simpler, and safer ways of operating. If you thrive in environments where people value learning and are committed to continuously improve daily operations, join us and be apart of our journey.

What We Can Offer

At APM Terminals, we foster a dynamic learning and training culture that empowers our employees to excel. Our commitment to improvement is driven by Lean principles, ensuring that every team member has the opportunity to develop their skills and advance their careers. Experience a diverse, multinational workplace where your operational insights directly influence how we work.

  • Work in a dynamic terminal environment supporting critical port and logistics operations.
  • Develop expertise through structured on-the-job learning, coaching, and HSE-focused development opportunities.
  • Build experience working with diverse stakeholders, contractors, regulatory agencies, and terminal operations teams.
  • Contribute to a culture of continuous improvement where safety, operational excellence, and people development are prioritized.

Key Responsibilities

  • Support the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the terminal's Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) Management System.
  • Conduct workplace inspections, safety audits, and compliance assessments, recommending and monitoring corrective actions.
  • Maintain awareness of emerging HSE regulations, industry standards, and best practices to strengthen operational safety and regulatory compliance.
  • Investigate incidents, near misses, unsafe acts, and unsafe conditions using root cause analysis and corrective action tracking.
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders, contractors, regulatory agencies, and external partners to promote a strong safety culture.
  • Maintain accurate HSE records, reports, and documentation while supporting compliance requirements.
  • Deliver HSE awareness and training initiatives for employees and third parties while supporting safe terminal operations on a 12-hour rotational shift schedule.

What We Are Looking For

  • Continuous improvement mindset: we are looking for someone who brings a thoughtful improvement mindset, curious about how work gets done and motivated to make meaningful, sustainable improvements over time.
  • A university degree, HND or its equivalent in Environmental Management, Engineering or any Health and Safety related fields.
  • NEBOSH and/or IOSH Certification is highly desirable. Active membership of ISPON is preferred.
  • Minimum three years of Health, Safety, and Environment experience, preferably within port operations, logistics, industrial, manufacturing, or heavy equipment environments.
  • Knowledge and practical experience in dangerous goods handling, emergency response, incident investigations, and risk assessments.
  • Strong communication, stakeholder management, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills.
  • Valid driver's license with the ability to operate within a dynamic port terminal environment.
  • Strong documentation, reporting, and Microsoft Office skills with a disciplined approach to regulatory compliance and operational safety.

title: Assistant Project Manager
description:
Who We Are:

For over 117 years and across four generations of family ownership, Brooks Construction Company, Inc. has stood for Family, Integrity, Respect, Safety, Teamwork, and Quality in the civil construction industry. Based in Fort Wayne, Indiana, with over 270 employees, Brooks Construction provides asphalt, concrete, earthwork, and pipe operations across northern Indiana and northwestern Ohio using best practices and innovative techniques to give our customers a quality product.

Job Summary

The Assistant Project Manager is responsible for supporting Project Management staff in coordinating and supervising construction activities across assigned projects, both in administrative and field roles. This individual will serve as a key resource to ensure projects are completed safely, on time, and within budget while meeting quality expectations. The role includes assisting in pre-construction tasks, jobsite support, logistics coordination, and documentation. Duties may also include site inspections, layout support, estimating assistance, and working with internal departments and external partners.

Essential Job Duties/Responsibilities

  • Picks up and delivers materials, tools, and equipment to various job sites
  • Sources and procures supplies from vendors, suppliers, or local retailers
  • Performs minor layout duties (e.g., layout of traffic control signs, white line areas for utility locates)
  • Takes and submits photos for project documentation (e.g., white line locates, end-of-project photos)
  • Helps clean completed job sites (e.g., pick up materials, remove signage, pull survey stakes, sweep sidewalks)
  • Performs general errands and site coordination tasks to support Project Managers
  • Assists with required inspections such as:
    • Traffic control devices
    • Stormwater / Erosion control
  • Confirms quantities on projects by visiting sites and measuring items of work
  • Assists with verifying sites are ready for Brooks' work and checking grades of previous work
  • Assists with pre-construction activities, including:
    • Field office setup
    • Bulletin board creation and setup
    • Borrow/disposal site submittals
    • Quality Control Plans
  • Assists sales/estimating team with quantity takeoffs for quotes on smaller projects
  • Begins reviewing contracts, specifications, and drawings to gain document familiarity
  • Assists in meetings with foremen on sites under the guidance of other Project Managers
  • Serves as vacation coverage for other team members as assigned

Other Duties/Responsibilities

  • Assist others in department as needed.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.

Required Skills and Abilities

  • Strong attendance, punctuality, reliability, and work ethic
  • Willingness to work evenings, weekends, and extended hours when needed
  • Valid driver's license and ability to travel within a 70-mile radius of the home office
  • Compliance with company Drug-Free & Alcohol-Free Workplace policies
  • Ability to wear personal protective equipment (PPE) as required
  • Comfortable in a fast-paced environment with minimal supervision
  • Demonstrated ability to learn quickly and follow procedures
  • Team-oriented with independent problem-solving skills
  • Demonstrated ability to work under the oversight and direction of other Project Managers
  • Willingness to observe and learn construction techniques and how to read specs/contracts
  • Demonstrated ability to read and understand blueprints (or willingness to learn)
  • Flexibility in managing multiple priorities within tight time constraints
  • High degree of accuracy, thoroughness, and attention to detail
  • Excellent interpersonal communication skills-both oral and written
  • Analytical and decision-making abilities
  • Proven dependability, organization, and adaptability skills
  • Ability to develop proficiency in key software programs-such as MS Outlook, MS Word, MS Excel, accounting software, Bluebeam, and the internal dashboard-through training provided by other Project Managers and/or formal classes

Education and Experience

  • High School Diploma or GED required
  • Minimum of 2 years' experience in a construction environment OR successful completion of a construction internship program
  • Previous hands-on experience in horizontal/civil construction is highly preferred

Physical Requirements

  • Lifting/Carrying: Up to 50 lbs. frequently
  • Pushing/Pulling: Up to 50 lbs. frequently
  • Driving: Regular driving of automatic and possibly standard transmission vehicles
  • Movement Requirements: Frequent standing, walking, bending, squatting, kneeling, twisting, and occasionally reaching above shoulder level, climbing and crawling
  • Use of Hands: Frequent use of hands for grasping, handling materials, and occasionally keyboarding

Working Environment

  • Works in a combination of office and field environments (50/50)
  • Ability to work in adverse conditions, including rain, snow, extreme heat or cold, water, mud, dust, etc.
  • Frequent interaction with internal team (Project Managers, Foremen, Superintendents, Estimators, Safety, Accounting) and external contacts (vendors, subcontractors, customers)

Supervisory Responsibilities

None

How to Apply:

Online: Visit to access our online Employment Application by clicking "View Open Positions and Apply Now!". Please include a resume if you have one.

Why Join Brooks Construction?

At Brooks Construction Company, we believe in building more than roads-we build careers, communities, and a legacy of excellence. Based in Fort Wayne, Indiana, with over 270 employees, Brooks Construction provides asphalt, concrete, earthwork, and pipe operations across northern Indiana and northwestern Ohio using best practices and innovative techniques to give our customers a quality product.

Our team-based approach ensures that every employee has the opportunity to make a meaningful impact. Whether you're starting your career or bringing years of experience, you'll find a supportive environment that values your contributions and fosters professional growth. ​

What We Offer – Non-Union Positions:

At Brooks Construction Company, we are proud to provide our employees with exceptional benefits that support their health, financial security, and overall well-being.​

Competitive Compensation:

  • Competitive pay
  • Opportunities for performance-based bonuses

Comprehensive Benefits:

  • Health Insurance - We pay 100% of the premium for you, your spouse and your eligible children)
  • Prescription Drug Plans, Dental and Vision Insurance
  • Health Savings Accounts – We make contributions on your behalf
  • Flexible Spending Accounts

Retirement & Financial Security:

  • 401K Plan – We contribute a portion of your 401K for you

Career Development:

  • Access to training programs and advancement opportunities

Join us in shaping the infrastructure of northern Indiana and northwestern Ohio. Be part of a team where ordinary people do things extraordinarily well. ​

title: Communications Specialist
description:
Position: Communications Specialist
Department: Marketing
Location: Wichita, KS (On-Site)
Job Type: Full-Time/Hourly
Jump start your career at Equity Bank! We are currently hiring energetic, team oriented, and community focused individuals to join our team! With a team of best-in-class customer service experts, you'll help to build and expand on client relationships, deliver the banking products and services that meet the unique and individual needs of clients, and create and uphold an atmosphere of superior experience and service. At Equity Bank we’ll help you invest in your community through volunteer opportunities which align with our company initiatives and core values.
Summary:
The Communications Specialist supports Equity Bank's internal and external communications, helping ensure clear, consistent, and timely messaging to employees, customers, and the communities the bank serves. This role plays a key part in supporting the bank's growth and integration efforts, including recent and upcoming acquisitions, by helping draft and coordinate employee announcements, customer communications, and public-facing messaging. This is an excellent opportunity for an early-career communications professional to build meaningful experience in a fast-growing community bank.
Responsibilities and Expectations
Key Responsibilities
  • Draft, edit, and coordinate internal communications, including employee announcements, newsletters, and updates related to company initiatives and organizational changes
  • Support the development of customer-facing communications, including notices related to promotions, product changes, and acquisition/integration milestones
  • Assist in drafting and maintaining internal FAQ documents to support employees and customer-facing teams during periods of change
  • Coordinate press release drafts and basic media inquiries in partnership with marketing leadership, ensuring consistent tone and messaging
  • Support the review and refinement of external-facing language for accuracy, clarity, and audience sensitivity — particularly for community banking and M&A-related communications
  • Maintain and update website and intranet content related to communications and company announcements
  • Assist with the coordination of internal communications calendars, ensuring messages are sequenced appropriately across audiences and channels
  • Support crisis or time-sensitive communications needs under the direction of marketing leadership
  • Write scripts for internal and external video content, partnering with the video/creative team to ensure messaging is clear and on-brand
  • Write and manage blog content that supports the bank's communications and content marketing goals
  • Provide copywriting support for advertising and promotional materials, ensuring consistent voice and messaging across channels
  • Partner with the broader marketing team on brand-consistent messaging across all communications materials
Required Skills & Education
Requirements
  • Bachelor's degree in Communications, Public Relations, Journalism, Marketing, or a related field
  • 2-4 years of experience in a communications, public relations, or marketing role
  • Strong writing and editing skills, with close attention to tone, accuracy, and audience, and the versatility to write across formats, including video scripts, blog content, and advertising copy
  • Ability to handle sensitive or confidential information with discretion, particularly around organizational change and M&A activity
  • Comfortable managing multiple deadlines and shifting priorities in a fast-paced environment
  • Experience with the banking or financial services industry is a plus but not required
Who We Are
Equity Bank, a full-service, $7.9 billion community bank, is based in Wichita, Kansas, with over 80 bank offices throughout Kansas, Nebraska, Missouri, Arkansas, and Oklahoma.
At Equity Bank, you can find exciting opportunities to challenge you, expand your skills, and reward your contributions. Our employees receive competitive compensation and benefits, while working in an atmosphere that encourages personal and professional growth. We’re searching for motivated individuals who are passionate about serving others, learning new technologies, and working as part of a team.
Equity Bank offers a full range of financial solutions, including online and mobile banking, commercial loans, consumer banking, and mortgage loans, treasury management service, the best solutions for your business, and absolutely zero ATM fees, anywhere.
What’s in it for you?
We believe your benefits are an important part of your overall compensation package. We work year-round to ensure that we provide our employees with the most up-to-date, competitive program. We thoroughly evaluate our benefit plans and strive to provide quality benefits that support the physical and financial well-being of our employees and their families.
Benefits Available:
  • Health, Dental & Vision Insurance
  • Group Life & Long-Term Disability Insurance
  • Flexible Spending & Health Savings Accounts
  • Group Cancer Insurance
  • 401(K) Retirement Plan w/Company Match
  • Generous Vacation & Sick Time
  • Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)
  • Pet Insurance
  • Retail Banking Benefits
Find your future at Equity Bank!
The above statements are intended to generally describe the nature and level of work to be performed by most people assigned to this job. It is not intended as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and requirements.
Physical Requirements
This position requires standing, walking, bending, and squatting on a regular basis. May require the ability to stoop, kneel, crouch or reach with hands and arms. Requires the ability to carry, lift, move or push up to 25 pounds on an occasional basis. Must be able to talk and listen to others.
Work Environment
This position regularly works in an office setting. Most of the job duties require the employee to be working with computers and electronic media on a regular basis.

description:
Pay Range: $59,984 - $77,979 annual compensation

Job Posting Closing on: Friday, October 2, 2026 📅

Benefits for this position include: 11 Paid Holidays, Medical, Dental, Vision, Paid Time Off, Pension Plan, Professional Development Opportunities. Find Out More!

The City of Fort Worth is one of the fastest growing large cities in the U.S. Our employees serve the needs of over 1,000,000 residents, promoting our values of exceptional customer experience, mutual respect, embracing our diversity, continuous improvement, ethical behavior, and accountability. 🌆

A Quality Control Specialist job is available with the City of Fort Worth Water Utility, Centralized Water Laboratory. This is a full-time position that supports the laboratory’s mission of providing accurate, responsive and cost-effective analytical and technical services to all areas of the community.

The Quality Control Specialist coordinates and monitors the city's laboratory or cities contract laboratory quality assurance activities for water, wastewater, pretreatment and environmental testing. Ensures compliance with all regulatory aspects of the Quality Assurance plan; and monitors, investigates and evaluates water quality programs, processes, and concerns.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university or college with major course work in Chemistry, Biology, Biochemistry, Environmental Engineering, or a related field and
  • Three (3) years of experience in laboratory or quality control/quality assurance operations, including water, wastewater or industrial pretreatment procedures
  • Valid Driver’s License
  • Must be able to pass Drug Screen

Preferred Qualifications:

  • One (1) year of experience working with TNI or TCEQ accreditation requirements or ISO/IEC 17025 laboratory quality standards
  • One (1) year of experience with state and/or federal regulations relating to water quality, such as the Safe Drinking Water Act or the Clean Water Act
  • Experience with laboratory information management systems (LIMS) and/or electronic quality management and data-management systems

The Quality Control Specialist job responsibilities include:

  • Develops, prepares and monitors the quality control and assurance plan for water, wastewater, pretreatment and environmental testing activities
  • Participates in internal and external audits, corrective actions, preventive actions, and studies regarding water, wastewater, and pretreatment quality assurance activities to ensure laboratory maintains compliance with regulatory requirements, which include Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) standards and The NELAC Institute (TNI) rules
  • Communicates effectively (both written and orally) with internal and external customers and maintain accurate and timely records
  • Interprets laboratory test results and sampling data; and maintains files of all monitoring activities and quality control documents
  • Develops and reviews Standard Operating Procedures (SOP’s); maintains inventory of logbooks, SOP’s and other controlled documents and oversees the archiving and destruction of laboratory documents in accordance with local, state and federal regulations
  • Investigates water quality problems in reservoirs, tributaries, treatment plants, distribution system and at customer city/industrial complexes; and assists users in resolving water quality and/or compliance issues
  • Estimates and projects needed funds regarding assigned quality control responsibilities; and coordinates and participates in procurement and calibration of monitoring devices and support equipment
  • Performs other related duties as required

Working Conditions and Physical Demands

Depending on assignment, positions in this class typically require touching, talking, hearing, seeing, grasping, standing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, reaching, walking, repetitive motions, climbing and balancing.

Light Work – Depending on assignment, positions in this class typically exert up to 20 pounds of force occasionally, up to 10 pounds of force frequently, and/or a negligible amount of force constantly having to move objects. If the use of arm and/or leg control requires exertion of forces greater than that for the Sedentary Work category and the worker sits most of the time, the job is rated Light Work.

Conditions of Employment

The City of Fort Worth is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. It is the policy and practice of the City to recruit, hire, train and promote a diverse workforce without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy and gender identity), national origin, political affiliation, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, genetic information, age, membership in an employee organization, parental status, military service, or another non-merit factor.

title: Year-Long Technology Internship (Summer 2027-Spring 2028)
description:
We are looking for motivated and talented students who want to help us solve some of the most complex challenges in financial technology. Technology teams at CME Group write and maintain ultra low-latency electronic trading platforms, risk management systems, and front-end trading interfaces, all of which are central to CME Group’s business. We are focused on designing, building, and deploying customer-focused solutions with passion and precision.

CME Group’s Technology Internship Program offers students opportunities to learn more about our enterprise, our role in the financial industry, and the types of technology that keep our markets running. Students will develop their technical skills and expand their network with access to industry experts, while working alongside other talented and ambitious students with a passion for FinTech.

Year-long interns will join in one of two areas:

  • Platform Engineer (Infrastructure focused)

  • Site Reliability Engineer (SRE)

Minimum qualifications:

  • Currently pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree in computer science or a related field

  • Experience writing code in Java and/or Python

  • Experience with cloud technologies

  • Passionate about problem solving and continuous learning

  • Detail-oriented

Preferred qualifications:

  • Previous technical experience

  • Experience with UNIX/Linux

  • Experience with powershell (windows)

  • Local Chicago candidates available to work in-office year-round

This focused year-round internship will begin in Summer 2027 at 40 hours a week in a hybrid role based in our Chicago office. Interns will then shift to part-time (about 15-20 hours a week) in Fall 2027 and Spring 2028. Local Chicago candidates who are available to work in-office year-round are preferred.

The summer program includes numerous opportunities to network with peers from across the country during a summer full of experiences such as excursions to enjoy Chicago traditions, trading and coding challenges with prizes, speaker series, and other opportunities for professional development.

As a platform intern, you will be working alongside CME's platform engineers to help create reliable processes and systems. This will be an infrastructure focused role with opportunities to learn about a variety of technologies, spanning fields such as automation, CI/CD, DevOps, and monitoring.

Focus:

  • System Design

  • Research and Proof of Concept

  • Automation

  • DevOps

  • Google Cloud, Kubernetes, Infrastructure

Bonus qualifications:

  • Proficiency in Python or bash shell (linux)

  • Experience with Google Cloud, Kubernetes, Cloud Infrastructure

This will be a development focused role with opportunities to learn about a variety of technologies, spanning fields such as big data, web development, automation and CI/CD, devops, and monitoring.

Focus:

  • Application Development

  • System Design

  • Research and Proof of Concept

  • DevOps and Cloud Migration

  • Automation

description:
End Date

Friday 18 September 2026

£0 - £0

We support flexible working – click here for more information on flexible working options

Hybrid Working, Job Share

Job Description Summary

JOB TITLE: Head of Pensions Investment & Funding
LOCATION(S): Edinburgh, Leeds, Halifax or Bristol
HOURS: Full-time
WORKING PATTERN: Our work style is hybrid, which involves spending at least two days per week, or 40% of our time, at one of our office sites.

Job Description

Are you passionate about delivering excellence in pensions investment and funding?

This is a fantastic opportunity to shape the future of our Defined Benefit (DB) and Defined Contribution (DC) schemes by leading our Pensions Investment and Funding Team of specialists, to develop and implement investment and funding strategies that deliver high-quality outcomes for our members.

Accountable to the Group Pensions Director and the Trustee, the role is responsible for the day-to-day oversight of the schemes’ investment and funding arrangements.

This is a senior role within the in-house Group Pensions Executive Team, supporting the Trustee on the most appropriate approach to funding and investment strategy and risk management, including the management of covenant risk. You act within parameters set by the Trustee covering hedging, liquidity, asset allocation, and the selection, monitoring and termination of Fund Managers. Accountability spans the Group’s main staff DB and DC pension schemes, for some 350,000 members with c£35bn in assets.

Day to day, you will

  • Maintain effective working relationships with the Trustee, Advisers, Fund Managers, Regulators and the Company.
  • Be responsible to the Group Pensions Director and to the Trustee for the effective and compliant management of c£35bn of assets and liabilities managed in the various Group pension schemes, within the delegated authorities set by the Trustee.
  • Support the Trustee in forming suitable strategic objectives and risk tolerance related to funding, investment and covenant to ensure alignment towards the long-term health of the schemes. This support is primarily through providing input to the Trustee’s strategic investment advisor on implementation considerations and, where appropriate, collaborative challenge on strategic thinking.
  • Work closely with the Chairs of the Investment and Funding Committee, Investment Oversight Committee and Trustee’s strategic investment advisor; to ensure effective delivery of the investment and funding strategies for the DB schemes, and facilitate engagement with the Group over future investment and funding strategies for the Schemes
  • Provide analysis, views and challenge to support the Trustee in developing, regularly reviewing and changing (when necessary) suitable investment strategies, such as hedging of key risks (LDI, FX, longevity), and the balance between different asset classes from across capital markets that are within the Trustee’s risk appetite.
  • Manage the portfolio within delegated authorities, maintaining hedges, maintaining the return potential at an acceptable level, responding to threats and opportunities, taking opportunities to de-risk as the Schemes become more mature.
  • Be accountable for execution and implementation of strategy, setting mandates, monitoring managers’ performance, holding managers to account, challenging managers on portfolio matters when required, as well as other key third party relationships. This involves ongoing collaboration with the Investment Operations Team.
  • Ensure delegated authorities remain appropriate for the effective ongoing management of the portfolio in line with the Trustee’s funding and investment strategy.
  • Maintain and manage liquidity, being aware of benefit payments, contributions, cash calls and other settlements.
  • Ensure the Trustee receives appropriate and timely advice on suitable DC investment strategies (eg default strategy, investment funds, portfolio construction) to reflect the Trustee’s overall DC objectives. Identify opportunities for reviewing and implementing changes to make sure fund choices for DC Scheme members remain appropriate.
  • Ensure a robust internal control environment exists, regarding taking of decisions, and implementation under delegated authority. Be responsible for the identification of emerging risks and implementation of effective risk management and de-risking strategies on behalf of the Trustee.
  • Supporting funding discussions with the Group on behalf of the Trustee, ensuring that outcomes remain appropriate within Trustee risk and long-term funding targets, and reflect regulatory guidance.
  • Collaborate with the Group on activities or opportunities impacting the funding position including asset performance, hedging, liquidity and collateral optimisation. Maximise opportunities to create value for the Schemes and work closely with the Group to identify synergies for mutual benefit.
  • Deliver regular performance, risk and management information and reports which enable the Trustee to provide appropriate oversight and enable the Group to understand the evolution of the financial position of the schemes and reflect its exposure to the Schemes’ liabilities through its financial and regulatory reporting.
  • Develop and maintain the Trustee’s policies in relation to responsible investment and the management of climate risk. Engage with the Trustee’s advisors on such matters, as relevant.
  • Lead and motivate a team of specialist investment professionals, setting an appropriate culture within the team, consistent with Group and Trustee values. Ensure resource remains appropriate to meet the Trustee’s requirements as they evolve.
  • Stay abreast of market developments.

What you'll need

  • Proven leader with demonstrable success in a large organisation, ideally with experience working for a major pension fund or in a senior investment role
  • Exceptional stakeholder management skills, able to manage relationships in a politically sensitive way, to balance and align stakeholders sometimes with conflicting objectives and confident engaging with senior stakeholders including trustees, advisers, providers, and within the Group.
  • Proven experience of navigating highly complex and technical pension funding and investment concepts, such as knowledge and understanding of liability structures and actuarial assumptions, broad investment knowledge across multiple asset classes and sub-classes, derivatives and leverage, portfolio construction, techniques to model liabilities and assets and to hedge risk, contingent capital arrangements.
  • Inspiring people leader and respected strategic thinker.
  • CFA or FIA qualification desirable.

We also offer a wide-ranging benefits package, which includes:

  • A generous pension contribution of up to 15%
  • An annual performance-related bonus
  • Share schemes including free shares
  • Benefits you can adapt to your lifestyle, such as discounted shopping
  • 30 days’ holiday, with bank holidays on top
  • A range of wellbeing initiatives and generous parental leave policies

About working for us

Our focus is to ensure we’re inclusive every day, building an organisation that reflects modern society and celebrates diversity in all its forms. We’re committed to creating a consciously inclusive workplace where our colleagues can be themselves, thrive and perform at their best. We were one of the first major organisations to set goals on diversity in senior roles, create a menopause health package, and a dedicated Working with Cancer Initiative.

As an inclusive employer, we offer Workplace Adjustments for colleagues with a disability (which may include long-term health and neurodivergent conditions) where it is reasonable to do so. This could include flexibility with regards to office attendance, location, and working pattern.

We also provide adjustments that are reasonable throughout the recruitment process to reduce or remove barriers for applicants with a disability, long-term health condition or neurodivergent condition. If you’d like an adjustment to the recruitment process just let us know

If you’re excited by the thought of becoming part of our team, get in touch. We’d love to hear from you.

10% Manuscripts and Scientific Communication: Prepare manuscripts for peer-reviewed publication and present research findings at laboratory meetings, scientific conferences, and other professional venues.

10% Research Planning and Grant Support: Review scientific literature, contribute to the development of research directions, and assist with preparation of research proposals and grant applications.

5% Laboratory Collaboration, Mentoring, and Operations: Collaborate with laboratory members and research partners; provide technical guidance and research mentoring to undergraduate and graduate students as appropriate; contribute to laboratory organization, maintenance of research materials and equipment, compliance with laboratory safety requirements, and other research-related duties as assigned.


Minimum Qualifications:
PhD in Plant Biology, Plant Science, Molecular Biology, Genetics, or a related field
